items.slavonic_text: Тво́й ды́мъ сле́зъ и҆спо́лни, бл҃гчести́выхъ ѻ҆́чи, но вѣ́тромъ Бж҃твенныхъ Оу҆чт҃ле́й, расточи́сѧ сꙋемꙋ́дрый І҆ѡа́нне :~
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Thou hast torn the divine robe, even as Arius tore the tunic of Christ of old; therefore art thou cast far from the Church, having been cast out like a dog![^909]

provenance.verbatim_source: *Troparion:* Thou hast torn the divine robe, even as Arius tore the tunic of Christ of old; therefore art thou cast far from the Church, having been cast out like a dog![^909]

items.office: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.season_or_tone: PART II: THE HOLY AND GREAT FORTY DAYS
items.day_or_date: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.slavonic_text: Ты ри́зꙋ Бж҃твеннꙋю растерза́лъ є҆сѝ, ꙗ҆́кѡже А҆́рїй пре́жде Хв҃ъ Хїтѡ́нъ. тѣ́мже ѿ цр҃кве дале́че ѿве́рженъ є҆сѝ, и҆зве́рженъ бы́въ ꙗ҆́кѡже пе́съ :~
items.english_text: *Triadikon:* As one Origin do I glorify the Godhead in three Hypostases; for God is one: Father, Son, and Spirit, even though distinguished in depictions and Persons!

provenance.verbatim_source: *Triadikon:* As one Origin do I glorify the Godhead in three Hypostases; for God is one: Father, Son, and Spirit, even though distinguished in depictions and Persons!

items.office: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.season_or_tone: PART II: THE HOLY AND GREAT FORTY DAYS
items.day_or_date: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.slavonic_text: Тр҃: Є҆ди́но нача́ло сла́влю Бж҃тва̀ въ трехъ ѷпо́стасехъ, є҆ди́нъ бо Бг҃ъ є҆́стъ Ѻ҆те́цъ, Сн҃ъ, и҆ Дх҃ъ, а҆́ще и҆ раздѣлѧ́ютсѧ И҆зѡбраже́ньми и҆ Ли́цы :~
items.english_text: *Theotokion:* Prophetically, O pure one glorious in God, hast thou appeared as the City of God, from which Thine own Creator was born, preserving thee after childbirth even as before!

provenance.verbatim_source: *Theotokion:* Prophetically, O pure one glorious in God, hast thou appeared as the City of God, from which Thine own Creator was born, preserving thee after childbirth even as before!

items.office: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.season_or_tone: PART II: THE HOLY AND GREAT FORTY DAYS
items.day_or_date: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.slavonic_text: Бг҃: Прр҃че́ски чт҃аѧ Бгосла́внаѧ, гра́дъ ꙗ҆ви́ласѧ є҆сѝ Бж҃їй, и҆з не́гоже роди́сѧ Са́мъ тво́рецъ тво́й, по рождествѣ́ тебѐ, ꙗ҆́кѡже пре́жде съхрани́въ :~
items.english_text: *Ode 7. Heirmos: "Unto those who have sinned and done iniquity":* The fire of heresies hath divine grace now extinguished, which burns the noetic Chaldeans, and bedews those who serve the Trinity, holding the praises throughout the four weeks![^910]

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Ode 7. Heirmos: "Unto those who have sinned and done iniquity":*  
The fire of heresies hath divine grace now extinguished, which burns the noetic Chaldeans, and bedews those who serve the Trinity, holding the praises throughout the four weeks![^910]

items.office: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.season_or_tone: PART II: THE HOLY AND GREAT FORTY DAYS
items.day_or_date: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.slavonic_text: Пѣ́снь, з҃. И҆рмо́: Съгрѣши́вшымъ и҆ бе: Жа́ръ є҆реті́й, ны́нѣ ᲂу҆гасе Бж҃твеннаѧ бл҃гть, палѧ́щаѧ ᲂу҆́мныхъ Халде́ѡвъ, и҆ ѡ҆роша́ющаѧ Тр҃ци слꙋжа́щихъ, четвери́чными Седми́цами, просла́вїи съдержа́щи.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* The Church is adorned, clothed, and beautified, bearing the depiction of the Incarnation of the Master of all, and His Passions and signs, fully according to divine laws!

provenance.verbatim_source: *Troparion:* The Church is adorned, clothed, and beautified, bearing the depiction of the Incarnation of the Master of all, and His Passions and signs, fully according to divine laws!

items.office: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.season_or_tone: PART II: THE HOLY AND GREAT FORTY DAYS
items.day_or_date: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.slavonic_text: И҆спестри́сѧ, ѡ҆блече́сѧ, ᲂу҆добри́сѧ Цр҃ковь, и҆зѡбраже́нїе Вл҃ки всѣ́хъ въплоще́нїѧ, и҆ стр҃тїй є҆гѡ̀ и҆ знаме́нїа носѧ́щи, в коне́цъ по Бж҃веннымъ зако́нам.
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Feast, celebrate, ye people of the Lord named after Christ, seeing the Church shone forth again with the beauty of the divine form, which He Who is God bore as man, in order to save us!

provenance.verbatim_source: *Troparion:* Feast, celebrate, ye people of the Lord named after Christ, seeing the Church shone forth again with the beauty of the divine form, which He Who is God bore as man, in order to save us!

items.office: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.season_or_tone: PART II: THE HOLY AND GREAT FORTY DAYS
items.day_or_date: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.slavonic_text: Пра́зднꙋйте, торжествꙋ́йте, Хр҃тоимени́тыи лю́дїе Гд҃ни, ви́дѧще цр҃ковь па́ки възсїѧ́вшꙋ, доброто́ю Бж҃твеннагѡ зра́ка, є҆го́же Бг҃ъ сы́й понесѐ ꙗ҆́кѡ чл҃вкъ, за є҆́же сп҃ти на́съ :~
items.english_text: *Troparion:* The Word suffered poverty, and hungered, and thirsted in the flesh; these are properties of human nature, whereby He is circumscribed, but He Himself is simple and uncircumscribed in Divinity!

provenance.verbatim_source: *Troparion:* The Word suffered poverty, and hungered, and thirsted in the flesh; these are properties of human nature, whereby He is circumscribed, but He Himself is simple and uncircumscribed in Divinity!

items.office: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.season_or_tone: PART II: THE HOLY AND GREAT FORTY DAYS
items.day_or_date: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.slavonic_text: Нищетвова̀, и҆ а҆́лкаше, и҆ жаждаше, пло́тїю Сло́во, Сїа̀ чл҃вче́скагѡ є҆щѐства сво́йства, и҆́миже ѡ҆писꙋ́етсѧ, Са́м же Бж҃твомъ просты́й є҆́стъ, и҆ неѡпи́санный :~
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Brought to naught are the phantasms and sorceries of the fighter against Christ; for equal unto the pagans did this writer appear in his frenzy, who unrighteously rejected also the voices of the Prophets!

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Troparion:* Brought to naught are the phantasms and sorceries...
...of the fighter against Christ; for equal unto the pagans did this writer appear in his frenzy, who unrighteously rejected also the voices of the Prophets!

items.office: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.season_or_tone: PART II: THE HOLY AND GREAT FORTY DAYS
items.day_or_date: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.slavonic_text: Хр҃тобо́рца, ра́венъ бо є҆́ллинѡмъ ꙗ҆ви́сѧ бѣснова́нїемъ, сїи списа́тель, ꙗ҆́же непра́веднѡ и҆ ѡ҆бро́си гла́сы прр҃кны́хъ :
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Thy secret, all-defiled, and soul-destroying teachings, what tongue can declare? Or the divination of thy sorcery, O falsely-named John, forerunner of the Antichrist of Satan![^911]

provenance.verbatim_source: *Troparion:* Thy secret, all-defiled, and soul-destroying teachings, what tongue can declare? Or the divination of thy sorcery, O falsely-named John, forerunner of the Antichrist of Satan![^911]

items.office: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.season_or_tone: PART II: THE HOLY AND GREAT FORTY DAYS
items.day_or_date: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.slavonic_text: Та́йнаѧ и҆ всескве́рнаѧ, и҆ дꙋшегꙋби́телнаѧ ᲂу҆че́нїѧ твоѧ̀, кі́й ꙗ҆зы́къ и҆сповѣ́сть! и҆ли́ прорече́нїе волшебства твоегѡ̀ І҆ѡа́нне лжеиме́нне, и҆ предоте́че А҆нті́христа сатаны̀ :~
items.english_text: *Troparion:* It befitted thee not, O lawless one, to be called by such a name, but rather Pythagoras, and Kronos, and Apollo, or some other of the gods, whose manner of life thou didst emulate, delighting in their impurities![^912]

provenance.verbatim_source: *Troparion:* It befitted thee not, O lawless one, to be called by such a name, but rather Pythagoras, and Kronos, and Apollo, or some other of the gods, whose manner of life thou didst emulate, delighting in their impurities![^912]

items.office: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.season_or_tone: PART II: THE HOLY AND GREAT FORTY DAYS
items.day_or_date: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.slavonic_text: Не подоба́ше тебѣ̀ ѽ беззако́нне и҆менова́тисѧ таковы́мъ нарица́нїемъ, но па́че Пѷѳаго́ромъ, и҆ Кро́номъ, и҆ А҆поллѡ́номъ, и҆ли́ нѣ́коимъ и҆ны́хъ бого́въ, и҆́хже житїю поревнова́лъ є҆сѝ, наслажда́ѧсѧ нечисто́тъ и҆́хъ : Сла́ва: Тр҃:
items.english_text: *Glory... Triadikon:* Unto the Co-eternal, All-powerful, Incomprehensible Trinity, all ye faithful, unto the Father, the Son, and the Spirit let us bow down; and in theology unconfusedly crying aloud: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O God!

provenance.verbatim_source: *Glory... Triadikon:* Unto the Co-eternal, All-powerful, Incomprehensible Trinity, all ye faithful, unto the Father, the Son, and the Spirit let us bow down; and in theology unconfusedly crying aloud: Holy, Holy, Holy art Thou, O God!

items.office: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.season_or_tone: PART II: THE HOLY AND GREAT FORTY DAYS
items.day_or_date: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.slavonic_text: Присносꙋ́щной, всеси́лной, непостижи́мой Тр҃ци вѣ́рнїи вси Ѻ҆ц҃ꙋ, Сн҃ꙋ, и҆ Дх҃ꙋ поклони́мсѧ. и҆ Бгослове́снѣмъ несли́тнѡ въззыва́юще, Ст҃ъ, Ст҃ъ, Ст҃ъ, є҆сѝ Бж҃е :~
items.english_text: *Both now... Theotokion:* All-hymned, most glorious Virgin, Mother and Theotokos, deliver from grievous transgressions those who honor thy most pure childbirth; for no other help besides thee have we acquired, O Bride of God!

provenance.verbatim_source: *Both now... Theotokion:* All-hymned, most glorious Virgin, Mother and Theotokos, deliver from grievous transgressions those who honor thy most pure childbirth; for no other help besides thee have we acquired, O Bride of God!

items.office: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.season_or_tone: PART II: THE HOLY AND GREAT FORTY DAYS
items.day_or_date: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.slavonic_text: Бг҃: Всепѣ́таѧ многосла́внаѧ Дв҃о Мт҃и Бгороди́тельнице, и҆зба́ви лю́тыхъ прегрѣше́нїй, чтꙋ́щыѧ твоѐ прчт҃ое рожде́нїе, и҆ны́ѧ бо по́мощи, кро́мѣ тебѐ Бгоневѣ́сто не стѧжа́хѡмъ :~
items.english_text: *Ode 8. Heirmos: "Him Whom the heavenly hosts glorify":* Prophetically let us rejoice and be glad, all ye faithful, mystically; for this is the day wherein Christ the Word gave His raiment unto the Church!

provenance.verbatim_source:
*Ode 8. Heirmos: "Him Whom the heavenly hosts glorify":*  
Prophetically let us rejoice and be glad, all ye faithful, mystically; for this is the day wherein Christ the Word gave His raiment unto the Church!

items.office: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.season_or_tone: PART II: THE HOLY AND GREAT FORTY DAYS
items.day_or_date: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.slavonic_text: Пѣ́снь, и҆. И҆рм: Є҆го́же во́и нб҃ныи слѧ́: Прр҃чески ра́дꙋимсѧ и҆ весели́мсѧ вѣ́рнїи вси та́иннѡ, се́н бо дн҃ь, во́ньже Хс҃ Сло́во, своѐ ѡ҆дѣѧ́нїе подадѐ цр҃кви :
items.english_text: *Troparion:* In martial array they set themselves against the form of Christ, with one soul, Lyzikos and John, a yoke of Belial, hewing the Church with the ax of malice!

provenance.verbatim_source: *Troparion:* In martial array they set themselves against the form of Christ, with one soul, Lyzikos and John, a yoke of Belial, hewing the Church with the ax of malice!

items.office: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.season_or_tone: PART II: THE HOLY AND GREAT FORTY DAYS
items.day_or_date: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.slavonic_text: Воинстве́ннѡ ѡ҆полчи́шасѧ на Хв҃ъ зра́къ, є҆динодꙋ́шнѡ Лѷсі́зхъ и҆ І҆ѡа́ннъ, сꙋпрꙋ́га велїа́рова, секи́рою зло́бы сѣкꙋ́ще цр҃ковь :~
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Who shall not weep over the great audacity of Lyzikos and John, beholding the divine form which was upon the Bronze Gate of the Palace being stoned by lawless men through the teaching of John?[^913]

provenance.verbatim_source: *Troparion:* Who shall not weep over the great audacity of Lyzikos and John, beholding the divine form which was upon the Bronze Gate of the Palace being stoned by lawless men through the teaching of John?[^913]

items.office: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.season_or_tone: PART II: THE HOLY AND GREAT FORTY DAYS
items.day_or_date: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.slavonic_text: Ка́кѡ неразꙋмѣ́лъ є҆сѝ слѣ́пче всеѡкаѧ́нный помраче́нный ᲂу҆мо́мъ, поне́бꙋ зрѧ̀ ᲂу҆краше́ннꙋю, Хв҃ымъ начерта́нїемъ, но самъ и҆мѣ́лъ є҆сѝ мꙋдрова́нїе І҆ꙋде́йское :
items.english_text: *Troparion:* How didst thou not understand, O blind man all-wretched, darkened in mind, seeing the sky adorned with the delineation of Christ; but thou thyself didst hold Jewish mindedness!

provenance.verbatim_source: *Troparion:* How didst thou not understand, O blind man all-wretched, darkened in mind, seeing the sky adorned with the delineation of Christ; but thou thyself didst hold Jewish mindedness!

items.office: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.season_or_tone: PART II: THE HOLY AND GREAT FORTY DAYS
items.day_or_date: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.slavonic_text: Ты въ коне́чнѡ разрꙋши́ти мнѣ́лъ є҆сѝ, Бж҃твенныхъ Црк҃ве́й плотодѣ́йщїй зра́къ Гд҃нь, и҆ ст҃ы́хъ всѣ́хъ, но Бж҃твеннаѧ блг҃ть разрꙋшѝ твоѐ мꙋчи́телство :
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Thou didst think utterly to destroy from the divine Churches the flesh-wrought form of the Lord and of all the Saints; but divine grace destroyed thy tyranny!

provenance.verbatim_source: *Troparion:* Thou didst think utterly to destroy from the divine Churches the flesh-wrought form of the Lord and of all the Saints; but divine grace destroyed thy tyranny!

items.office: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.season_or_tone: PART II: THE HOLY AND GREAT FORTY DAYS
items.day_or_date: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.slavonic_text: Сщ҃е́ннымъ мо́щемъ ст҃ы́[хъ], и҆ И҆́кѡнамъ и҆́хъ Ли́зизхъ люты́й вкꙋ́пѣ съ І҆ѡа́нномъ ве́лѧчески непокланѧ́тисѧ, реко́ста беззако́ннѡ, ѿме́тника Блг҃ттїѧ :~
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Unto the sacred relics of the Saints and unto their Icons, fierce Lyzikos together with John expressly commanded not to bow down, speaking lawlessly, the apostates from piety![^914]

provenance.verbatim_source: *Troparion:* Unto the sacred relics of the Saints and unto their Icons, fierce Lyzikos together with John expressly commanded not to bow down, speaking lawlessly, the apostates from piety![^914]

items.office: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.season_or_tone: PART II: THE HOLY AND GREAT FORTY DAYS
items.day_or_date: The Order on the Sunday of Orthodoxy: For the Anathema of Heretics
items.slavonic_text: Тр҃: Вседѣ́телное Бгонача́лїе почита́юще, въ начерта́нїихъ тре́хъ вси блг҃чтно, безна́чалнагѡ Ѻ҆ц҃а̀, събезна́чалнаго Сло́ва, Дх҃а съпросїѧ́ющаго, просла́вимъ въ вѣ́ки :~
items.english_text: *Triadikon:* Honoring the all-effecting Godhead in three Persons, all of us piously, let us glorify unto ages of ages the beginningless Father, the co-beginningless Word, and the co-shining Spirit!

provenance.verbatim_source: *Triadikon:* Honoring the all-effecting Godhead in three Persons, all of us piously, let us glorify unto ages of ages the beginningless Father, the co-beginningless Word, and the co-shining Spirit!

items.english_text: *Theotokion:* A sure bridge for Christians, the boast of the faithful, and refuge, O Sovereign Lady Theotokos, thou art the sole helper of all, and the one who saves from perils!

items.slavonic_text: Пѣ́снь, ѳ҃. И҆рмо́. Безнасѣ́менна зача́тїа: Ꙗ҆зы́цы плещи́те, ли́цы Ѻ҆те́цъ потщи́тесѧ, По́стницы же сꙋ́щїи в гора́хъ сниди́тесѧ, прїидѣ́те и҆згна́нныи дре́вле ѿ ле́стиваго и҆ злочести́вагѡ І҆ѡа́нна, ѡ҆бличи́ти волхвова́нїа, и҆ чарова́нїа :~
items.english_text: *Ode 9. Heirmos: "A conception without seed":* Clap your hands, ye nations! Make haste, ye choirs of Fathers! And ye ascetics who are in the mountains, assemble; come, ye who were exiled of old by deceitful and impious John, to expose his sorceries and enchantments!

provenance.verbatim_source:

Clap your hands, ye nations! Make haste, ye choirs of Fathers! And ye ascetics who are in the mountains, assemble; come, ye who were exiled of old by deceitful and impious John, to expose his sorceries and enchantments!

items.slavonic_text: Весели́сѧ пꙋсты́ни, и҆ вселе́ннаѧ всѧ̀, го́ры всѧ̀ сла́дость и҆скапи́те, хо́лми възра́дꙋйтесѧ, ꙗ҆́кѡ Хс҃ Сло́во ми́ръ дадѐ сꙋ́щымъ на землѝ, и҆ Бж҃твеннымъ Цр҃квамъ є҆ди́нство вѣ́ры :~
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Rejoice, O wilderness, and all the inhabited world! All ye mountains, drop down sweetness, ye hills, be glad; for Christ the Word hath given peace unto those on earth, and unity of faith unto the divine Churches!

items.english_text: *Troparion:* The God of consecrations hath now boldly proclaimed, most holy Christ, strengthening today the divine Teachers with boldness to speak, that His condescension and Incarnation be surely depicted upon the Icon!

items.slavonic_text: Долготерпѣли́ве Гд҃и, коль чꙋ́днаѧ дѣла̀ твоѧ̀! кто и҆зчте́тъ чл҃колꙋ́бїе твоѐ; ка́кѡ зрѧ̀ ᲂу҆бива́емыхъ по ѡ҆́бразꙋ твое́мꙋ сщ҃е́нникѡвъ и҆ по́стникѡ, не ѡ҆пали́ши ле́стивыхъ, но претерпѣва́еши досажда́ем:
items.english_text: *Troparion:* O longsuffering Lord, how marvelous are Thy works! Who can recount Thy love for mankind? How, beholding priests and ascetics slain according to Thine image, didst Thou not consume the deceitful ones with fire, but didst endure being insulted?[^915]

items.slavonic_text: Въздрꙋзи́вый подвижи́мꙋю Цр҃ковь Гд҃и, и҆ вра́та а҆́довы сеѧ̀ невъзмого́ша, Са́мъ ми́ръ тво́й пода́ждь лю́демъ твои́мъ, да тебѣ̀ вси чти́тѣ, въ є҆ди́номъ славосло́вїи покланѧ́емсѧ, и҆ сла́вимъ :
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Thou Who didst establish the immovable Church, O Lord, and the gates of hades could not prevail against her, do Thou Thyself grant Thy peace unto Thy people, that honoring Thee, we may all bow down and glorify Thee in one doxology!

items.slavonic_text: Проклѧ́ти да бꙋ́дꙋтъ, не чтꙋ́щїи Вл҃ко начерта́нїа пло́ти твое́ѧ, пре́жде всѣ́хъ І҆ѡа́ннъ вкꙋ́пѣ съ А҆нтѡ́нїемъ, и҆ Ѳео́дѡромъ злочести́вымъ Ѳеодо́томъ, и҆ и҆ны́ми гꙋби́телми вѣ́ры :~
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Accursed be they who honor not the delineations of Thy flesh, O Master, before all others John, together with Antony, and Theodore, and impious Theodotos, and the other destroyers of the faith![^916]

items.slavonic_text: Да́ѧй ми́ръ тво́й А҆пл҃ѡмъ Вл҃ко, и҆ ны́нѣ пода́ждь, тишинꙋ̀ всѣ́мъ, събира́ѧ рꙋко́ю свое́ю расточе́нныѧ, и҆ ꙗ҆́кѡже ѻ҆вца̀ слове́сныѧ съчинѝ ѡ҆гра́дѣ, ст҃ы́ѧ Цр҃кве твое́ѧ :~ Сла́ва: Трїи́ч:
items.english_text: *Troparion:* Thou Who gavest Thy peace unto the Apostles, O Master, grant now also tranquility unto all, gathering with Thy hand those who are scattered, and assemble them like spiritual sheep into the sheepfold of Thy holy Church!

items.slavonic_text: Сла́влю Бж҃тво̀ Ѻ҆ц҃а̀, Сн҃а, и҆ Дх҃а, є҆ди́но є҆ст҃тво̀, въ тре́хъ ѷпоста́сехъ сꙋ́щество нераздѣ́лное, раздѣ́лное ли́цы, є҆диноцр҃твенное, вседѣ́телное, съверше́ное нача́лное, съдержа́щее всѧ́ческаѧ : Бг҃:
items.english_text: *Glory... Triadikon:* I glorify the Godhead of the Father, the Son, and the Spirit, one nature in three Hypostases, an indivisible essence, distinct in Persons, of one sovereignty, all-effecting, perfect, primal, upholding all things!

items.slavonic_text: Кли́къ Прр҃кѡвъ, съ Мѡѷсе́емъ и҆ А҆арѡно́[мъ], весе́лїемъ весели́сѧ дне́сь, ꙗ҆́кѡ коне́цъ Прр҃чества̀ приводѧ̀, свѣ́титъ Кр҃тъ, на не́мже насъ сп҃слъ є҆сѝ. тѣ́хъ мл҃твами Хе҃ Бж҃е сп҃си дꙋ́ша на́ша :~

items.slavonic_text: До́лжное къ Бг҃ꙋ лѣ́тное блг҃даре́нїе, во́нже дн҃ь прїѧ́хѡ[мъ] Бж҃їю Цр҃ковь, съ показа́нїемъ блг҃чтїѧ дѡ́гматъ, и҆ посрамле́нїемъ зло́бы злочествꙋ́ющыхъ.
items.english_text: Following the prophetic utterances, and conforming ourselves unto the apostolic teachings, and being instructed by the evangelical narratives, we celebrate the Day of Dedication.[^919] For Isaiah said: *Keep dedication toward God, ye islands* (Isa. 41:1), enigmatically signifying the churches from among the Gentiles. Now the churches were not simply the structures and embellishments of temples, but the fulness of those who practice piety within them, and wherewith they serve the Godhead with hymns and doxologies.

items.slavonic_text: Проро́ческимъ послѣ́дꙋюще рече́нїемъ, А҆пл҃кимъ же ᲂу҆чн҃їемъ подоба́ющесѧ: и҆ є҆ѵл҃скими повѣ́стми ᲂу҆ча́щесѧ, Ѽбновле́нїй Дн҃ь пра́зднꙋемъ. И҆са́їа бо речѐ: Ѽбновлѧ́йтесѧ Ѻ҆строви къ Бг҃ꙋ: ѿ Ꙗ҆зы́кѡвъ Цр҃квы гада́телствꙋѧ. Бѣ́ша же ᲂу҆́бѡ Цр҃квы не про́стѡ хра́мѡ зда́нїа, и҆ свѣтли́ванїа, но въ тѣ́хъ блг҃чтвꙋющїй и҆сполне́нїе, и҆ и҆́ми же ѡ҆нѝ Бж҃твꙋ, пѣ́сньми и҆ славосло́вїи слꙋ́жатъ. А҆́пл҃ъ же само́мꙋ семꙋ̀ ᲂу҆ча̀, въ ѡ҆бновле́нїи жи́зни ходи́ти, повелѣва́етъ. И҆ а҆́ще ка́ѧ въ Хѣ̀ но́ваѧ тва́рь, ѡ҆бновлѧ́тисѧ. И҆ словеса́ же Гд҃нѧ, Прр҃ческое пока́зꙋющи ᲂу҆мышле́нїе: Бы́ша, речѐ, ѡ҆бновле́нїа въ І҆ерл҃имѣхъ, и҆ зима̀ бѣ̀. И҆лѝ ᲂу҆́бѡ мы́слнаѧ, вню́же ро́дъ І҆ꙋде́йскїй, на ѻ҆́бщагѡ сп҃са, скверноᲂу҆бі́йства повѧза́ша сѣ́рпъ же и҆ мо́лвꙋ. И҆лѝ и҆ ѡ҆скорблѧ́ющаѧ тѣле́снаѧ чꙋ́вьства премѣне́нїемъ возду́ха на зимно́сть. Бы́стьже ᲂу҆́бѡ и҆ на на́съ зима̀, неприлꙋ́чшаѧсѧ, но вои́стиннꙋ, вели́каѧ зло́бы, и҆злива́ющаѧ сꙋро́вство: Но процвѣтѐ на́мъ блг҃тїй Бж҃їй превѣ́чнаѧ весна̀, вню́же блг҃рное жни́во въ блг҃и́хъ Бг҃ꙋ снидо́хѡмсѧ сътвори́ти. ꙗ҆́кѡ да рече́мъ Ѱало́мское: Лѣ́то и҆ Веснꙋ̀, ты съсъзда́лъ є҆сѝ сїа̀, помѧнѝ сеѧ̀. Вои́стиннꙋ бо поноша́ющыхъ, Гдⷭ҇а, врагѡ́въ, и҆ сегѡ́ ст҃о́е поклоне́нїе въ сты́хъ И҆́кѡнахъ безче́ствовавшыи, възви́женныхъ же и҆ възнесе́нныхъ, злоче́стїи, низве́рже и҆́хъ, чꙋдесе́мъ Бг҃ъ, и҆ ѿстꙋпле́нїа шата́нїа на земли попра̀, ни́же презрѣ̀ гла́са вопїю́щихъ к не́мꙋ: Помѧнѝ Гд҃и поноше́нїа рабѡ́въ твои́хъ, є҆го́же ᲂу҆держа́лъ є҆сѝ в нѣ́дрѣ мое́мъ мнѡ́гихъ ꙗ҆зы́кѡвъ, и҆́миже поноси́ша вра́зи твои́ Гд҃и, и҆́миже поноси́ша и҆змѣне́нїю Хрїста̀ твое́гѡ. И҆змѣне́нїе же ᲂу҆́бѡ бя́ше Хв҃о, сме́ртїю є҆гѡ̀ и҆скꙋ́пленныи, и҆ вѣ́ровавшїи є҆мꙋ̀, сло́вомъ же Про́повѣди, и҆ И҆́кѡннымъ и҆зѡбраже́нїемъ, и҆́миже ве́лїе дѣ́ло смотре́нїа
items.english_text: And the Apostle, teaching this very thing, commands us to walk in newness of life (Rom. 6:4); and if anyone be a new creature in Christ, to be renewed (2 Cor. 5:17).

provenance.verbatim_source: And the Apostle, teaching this very thing, commands us to walk in newness of life (Rom. 6:4); and if anyone be a new creature in Christ, to be renewed (2 Cor. 5:17).

Бы́стьже ᲂу҆́бѡ и҆ на на́съ зима̀, неприлꙋ́чшаѧсѧ, но вои́стиннꙋ, вели́каѧ зло́бы, и҆злива́ющаѧ сꙋро́вство: Но процвѣтѐ на́мъ блг҃тїй Бж҃їй превѣ́чнаѧ весна̀, вню́же блг҃рное жни́во въ блг҃и́хъ Бг҃ꙋ снидо́хѡмсѧ сътвори́ти. ꙗ҆́кѡ да рече́мъ Ѱало́мское: Лѣ́то и҆ Веснꙋ̀, ты съсъзда́лъ є҆сѝ сїа̀, помѧнѝ сеѧ̀. И҆змѣне́нїе же ᲂу҆́бѡ бя́ше Хв҃о, сме́ртїю є҆гѡ̀ и҆скꙋ́пленныи, и҆ вѣ́ровавшїи є҆мꙋ̀, сло́вомъ же Про́повѣди, и҆ И҆́кѡннымъ и҆зѡбраже́нїемъ, и҆́миже ве́лїе дѣ́ло смотре́нїа
items.english_text: And the words of the Lord also indicate the prophetic intention: *It was,* He says, *the Feast of Dedication in Jerusalem, and it was winter* (John 10:22). Either a spiritual winter, wherein the Jewish race bound the sickle of foul murder and turmoil against the common Savior; or that which grieves the bodily senses by the change of the air unto coldness. And there was indeed upon us also a winter, not accidental, but truly a great winter of malice, pouring forth cruelty. But there hath blossomed forth for us by the grace of God an eternal spring, wherein we have come together to produce a thankful harvest in good deeds unto God!

items.english_text: So that we may say the words of the Psalm: *Summer and spring, Thou hast formed them; remember this* (Ps. 73[74]:17–18). For in truth the enemies who reproached the Lord, and who dishonored His holy veneration in the holy Icons, who were haughty and exalted in impiety, God cast them down with wonders, and trod underfoot upon the earth the insolence of their apostasy!

items.english_text: Nor did He despise the voice of those who cry aloud unto Him: *Remember, O Lord, the reproach of Thy servants, which I have held in my bosom, of many nations, wherewith Thine enemies have reproached, O Lord, wherewith they have reproached the footsteps of Thine Anointed* (Ps. 88[89]:51–52).[^920] Now the recompense of Christ was those who were redeemed by His death and who believed in Him, both by the word of the Preaching and by the depiction of the Icons, whereby the great work of the Dispensation is made known unto those who are redeemed: by the Cross, and before the Cross, and after the Cross, and by His Passions and miracles. From which also the imitation of His Passions passes over unto the Apostles, and thence unto the Martyrs, and through them it extends even unto the Confessors and Ascetics.

items.slavonic_text: и҆збавлє́ннымъ познава́етсѧ: Кр҃то́мъ же и҆ пре́жде Кр҃та̀, и҆ по Кр҃тѣ, Стр҃тми же и҆ чꙋдесы̀ є҆гѡ̀. Ѿни́хже, и҆ подража́нїе стр҃тїй є҆гѡ̀ на А҆пл҃ы, ѿтꙋ́дꙋ же на Мч҃нки прехо́дитъ. и҆ тѣ́ми, да́же до И҆сповѣ́дникѡвъ и҆ По́стникѡвъ прихо́дитъ.
items.english_text: Remembering this reproach, therefore, wherewith the enemies of the Lord reproached, wherewith they reproached the recompense of His Christ, our God, being appeased by His compassion and inclined by the prayers of His Mother, and furthermore by those of the Apostles and of all the Saints who were likewise insulted together with Him and dishonored in the Icons; that just as they suffered in the flesh, so also, as was fitting, they who shared in the insults against the venerable Icons should be judged at last; when He willed it, He hath accomplished today a second time that which He performed at first!

items.slavonic_text: Сегѡ̀ ᲂу҆́бѡ поноше́нїа, и҆́мже поноси́ша вра́зи Гд҃ни, и҆́мже поноси́ша и҆змѣне́нїю Хв҃ є҆гѡ̀, въспомѧнꙋ́въ Бг҃ъ на́шъ, свои́мъ мл҃рдїемъ ᲂу҆мля́емъ, и҆ Мт҃ре свое́ѧ мл҃твами прекланѧ́емъ. Є҆ще́же и҆ А҆пл҃кими, и҆ всѣ́хъ ст҃ы́хъ, и҆́же и҆ вкꙋ́пѣ с ни́мъ досажде́ни бы́ша, но ᲂу҆ничиже́ни бы́ша на И҆́кѡнехъ. Да ꙗ҆́кѡже съвръша̀ пло́тїю, та́кѡ ᲂу҆́бѡ ꙗ҆́кѡже подоба́ше, и҆ сꙋ́ще ѡ҆ чт҃ны́ И҆́кѡнахъ є҆мꙋ̀ съвѣща́вшасѧ, доса́дами сꙋдѧ́й послѣ́днїи, є҆гда̀ въсхотѣ̀ дне́сь, и҆ сꙋдѣ́ла вто́рое, є҆́же съвръшѝ пе́рвѣе. Пе́рвѣе же ᲂу҆́бѡ, по многолѣ́тномъ нѣ́коемъ вре́мени ᲂу҆ничиже́нїа, и҆ безче́стїа сты́хъ И҆́коносовъ, възвратѝ въ блг҃чтїе своѐ: Нн҃ѣ же, є҆́же є҆́стъ вто́рое, ма́ло по три́десѧти лѣ́тъ ѡ҆ѕлобле́нїа, сꙋдѣ́ла недосто́йнымъ намъ злоде́нствъ премѣне́нїе, и҆ печа́лнꙋющыхъ и҆збавлѐнїе, и҆ блг҃тїѧ проповѣда́нїе, и҆ И҆́кѡннагѡ поклоне́нїа и҆звѣще́нїе, и҆ всѧ̀ сп҃сеннаѧ на́мъ носѧ́щїи пра́здни. На И҆́кѡнѣхъ бо зри́мъ Вл҃чнїа ѡ҆ на́съ стр҃ти, Кр҃тъ, Гро́бъ, а҆́дъ ᲂу҆мерщвле́нный и҆ раздрꙋше́ный. Мч҃никѡвъ по́двиги, вѣ́нцы, са́мое сп҃нїе: є҆гѡ́же пе́рвый на́шъ Подвигополо́жникъ, и҆ подвигода́тел, и҆ вѣ́нчикъ посредѣ̀ землѧ̀ съдѣ́ла̀. Сїѐ дне́сь торжество̀ пра́зднꙋемъ. к сїѐ мл҃твами и҆ моле́ньми съра́дꙋющесѧ и҆ съвеселѧ́щесѧ, ѱа́лмы и҆ пѣ́сньми възопїе́мъ: Внѣ̀, три́щи.
items.english_text: For at first indeed, after a certain time of many years of humiliation and dishonor of the holy Icons, He restored them unto His piety;[^921] and now, which is the second time, after nearly thirty years of affliction, He hath wrought for us unworthy ones a change from evil days, and deliverance for those in sorrow, and the proclamation of piety, and the confirmation of the veneration of Icons, and a festival bearing unto us all things conducive unto salvation![^922]

items.english_text: For upon the Icons we behold the Master's Passions for our sake: the Cross, the Tomb, hades slain and destroyed, the contests of the Martyrs, their crowns, and salvation itself, which our first Contest-master, Contest-giver, and Crowner wrought in the midst of the earth! This celebration do we observe today; and rejoicing and being glad therein with prayers and supplications, let us cry aloud with psalms and hymns:

items.slavonic_text: Но ᲂу҆́бѡ къ Бг҃ꙋ блг҃ре́нїе, и҆ вл҃чнаѧ на проти́вныхъ побѣ́да, вси́хъ. по́двиги же и҆ боре́нїа на И҆кѡнобо́рцѡвъ, и҆но́е сло́во и҆ словописа́нїе простра́ннѣйшее ꙗ҆ви́тъ. ꙗ҆́кѡ въ ᲂу҆покое́нїи же нѣ́коемъ по пꙋсты́нномъ преше́ствїи, въ ѡ҆держа́нїе мы́слднагѡ І҆ерл҃има ста́вше, Мѡѷсе́енскимъ нѣ́кимъ подража́нїемъ, па́че же Бж҃кїимъ повелѣ́нїемъ, ꙗ҆́кѡже столпꙋ̀ нѣ́коему ѿ велича́йши[хъ] ка́менїй съчинѐнномꙋ, и҆ къ прїѧ́тїю писа́нїа приложе́нномꙋ ср҃дцамъ бра́тїй. items.english_text: Now thanksgiving unto God and the Master's victory over the adversaries belong unto all; but the contests and struggles against the iconoclasts, another and more extensive treatise and narrative shall show forth. As in a certain rest after wandering in the wilderness, standing in possession of the spiritual Jerusalem, in a certain imitation of Moses, and yet more by divine command (cf. Deut. 27:1–8), as upon a certain pillar composed of the greatest stones, and adapted for the reception of writing for the hearts of the brethren: the blessings which are due unto the keepers of the Law, and the curses which the transgressors bring upon themselves, we have deemed it righteous and incumbent upon us to write down. Therefore let us say these things:

items.slavonic_text: Вѣ́дꙋщи Хв҃ы є҆ди́ный и҆ то́йже ѷпо́стаси, въ сꙋ́ществахъ и҆́ныхъ, създа́нное и҆ несѣзда́нное, ви́димое и҆ неви́димое, стра́стное и҆ безстра́стное, ѡ҆пи́санное и҆ неѡпи́санное, и҆ Бж҃кїимъ ᲂу҆́бѡ сꙋщество́мъ, нессъда́нное и҆ подоба́ющаѧ прилага́ющымъ, чл҃в́чкмъ же є҆ст҃твомъ и҆на́ѧ ѡ҆пи́санное и҆сповѣ́дꙋщымъ, и҆ сло́вомъ и҆зѡбразꙋ́ющимъ: Вѣ́чнаѧ па́мѧть. три́жды.

items.slavonic_text: Сло́вомъ ѡ҆сщ҃а́ющимъ ᲂу҆стнѣ̀, та́же слы́шателе ра́ди сло́ва, вѣ́дꙋщїй же и҆ проповѣ́дающїй, ꙗ҆́кѡ ѡ҆сщ҃а́тсѧ ᲂу҆́бѡ та́кожде ра́ди чт҃ны́хъ И҆́кѡнъ ѻ҆́чїи зрѧ́щи, въздви́жит же сѧ тѣ́ми ᲂу҆́мъ къ Бг҃овидѣ́нїю, ꙗ҆́кѡже Бж҃твенными Хра́мы, и҆ сщ҃енными сосꙋ́ды, и҆ и҆ны́ми требова́нїи: Вѣ́чнаѧ па́мѧть. три́жды.

items.slavonic_text: Прр҃ческаѧ видѣ́нїа, ꙗ҆́кѡже са́мое бж҃тво̀ и҆́хъ и҆зѡбразѝ, и҆ начерта̀. вѣ́дꙋщымъ, и҆ прїе́млющымъ, и҆ вѣ́рꙋющымъ, ꙗ҆́же Прр҃ческі́й ли́къ ви́дѣвше и҆сповѣ́даша. и҆ А҆пл҃ы, и҆ на Ѻ҆ц҃ы преше́дше преда́нїе написа́нїемъ, и҆ неписа́нное держа́щымъ, и҆ сегѡ́ ра́ди и҆зѡбразꙋ́ющымъ ст҃аѧ, и҆ почита́ющымъ: Вѣ́чнаѧ па́мѧть. г҃.

items.slavonic_text: Ра́зꙋмѣ́ющимъ Мѡѷсе́а гл҃юща, Внемлѣ́те себѣ̀ ꙗ҆́кѡ въ дн҃ь, во́ньже гла̀ Гд҃ь Бг҃ъ к Хѡри́вѣ на Го́рѣ, гла́съ ᲂу҆́бѡ слове́съ ᲂу҆слышасте вы, подо́бїа же не ви́дите. и҆ вѣ́дꙋщымъ ѿвѣща́ти пра́во. А҆́ще же ви́димъ нѣ́что, вои́стиннꙋ же ви́димъ, ꙗ҆́кѡже Сн҃ъ Гро́мовъ насъ наꙋчѝ: Є҆́же бѣ̀ и҆спе́рва, є҆́же слы́шахѡмъ, є҆́же ви́дѣхѡмъ, є҆́же ᲂу҆зрѣ́хѡмъ ѻ҆чи́ма на́шима, и҆ рꙋ́ки на́ши ѡ҆сѧза́ша ѡ҆ слове́си живо́тномъ. и҆ сїа̀ свидѣ́телствꙋемъ. И҆ па́ки ꙗ҆́кѡже и҆ны́и сло́ва ᲂу҆чн҃цы: Ꙗ҆до́хѡмъ с ни́мъ, и҆ пи́хѡ[мъ]. Не пре́жде стр҃ти то́кмѡ, но и҆ по стр҃ти и҆ въскрнїи. Ѿ Бг҃а ᲂу҆́бѡ показа́ти ᲂу҆крѣпле́ннымъ въ Зако́нѣ ѡ҆сщ҃а́нїе, и҆ къ блг҃ти ᲂу҆че́нїе. И҆ въ ѻ҆́номъ ᲂу҆́бѡ неви́димое, в се́мже, и҆ ви́димое
items.english_text: Unto those who know that the Rod, and the Tablets, the Ark, and the Candlestick, and the Table, and the Censer, prefigured and foreshadowed the Virgin and Theotokos Mary; and that while these things indeed prefigured her, she was not those things; but she was a Maiden, and remains a Virgin after the birth of God; and who therefore rather depict this Maiden in likenesses, or foreshadow her in outlines:

items.english_text: Unto those who understand Moses saying: *Take heed unto yourselves, for on the day when the Lord God spoke at Horeb on the mountain, ye heard the voice of words, but saw no similitude* (Deut. 4:12, 15); and who know how to answer rightly: If we see anything, we truly see it, even as the Son of Thunder taught us: *That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen, which we have looked upon with our eyes, and our hands have handled, of the Word of life; and these things we testify* (1 John 1:1–2);[^923] and again, as the other disciples of the Word said: *We ate and drank with Him* (Acts 10:41), not only before the Passion, but also after the Passion and Resurrection: in order that by God there might be shown unto those confirmed in the Law a sanctification, and a teaching toward grace; and that in the former indeed was the invisible, but in the latter also the visible and sensible; and who therefore depict and bow down before things seen and sensible:

items.slavonic_text: Про́роцы ꙗ҆́кѡже ви́дѣша. А҆́пл҃ы ꙗ҆́кѡже наꙋчи́ша. Цр҃квъ ꙗ҆́кѡже прїѧ́тъ. Оу҆чт҃ли ꙗ҆́кѡже повелѣ́ша. Вселе́ннаѧ ꙗ҆́кѡже сꙋмꙋ́дрꙋѧ. Блг҃ть ꙗ҆́кѡже възсїѧ̀. И҆́стина ꙗ҆́кѡже показа́сѧ. Ло́жь ꙗ҆́кѡже поги́бе. Премꙋ́дрость ꙗ҆́кѡже ѡ҆долѣ̀. Хс҃ ꙗ҆́кѡже повелѣ̀. Та́кѡ мꙋ́дрꙋемъ, та́кѡ гл҃емъ, та́кѡ проповѣ́дꙋемъ Ха́ и҆́стиннаго Бг҃а на́шегѡ, и҆ ст҃ы́хъ є҆гѡ̀, въ словесе́хъ почита́юще: въ списа́нїихъ, ᲂу҆мышле́нїихъ, въ же́ртвахъ, въ хра́мѣхъ, въ и҆зѡбраже́нїихъ. томꙋ́ ᲂу҆́бѡ ꙗ҆́кѡ Бг҃ꙋ, и҆ Вл҃цѣ поклана́ющесѧ, и҆ чтꙋ́ще. тѣ́хже ра́ди ѻ҆́бщаго Вл҃ки, ꙗ҆́кѡ бли́жайши є҆гѡ̀ рабѡ́въ, почита́юще, и҆ по ᲂу҆держа́нїи поклоне́нїе подаю́ще.
items.english_text: As the Prophets saw, as the Apostles taught, as the Church received, as the Teachers commanded, as the inhabited world agrees, as grace shone forth, as truth was shown, as falsehood perished, as wisdom prevailed, as Christ ordained: thus do we mind, thus do we speak, thus do we proclaim Christ our true God, and His Saints, honoring them in words, in writings, in thoughts, in sacrifices, in temples, in depictions; bowing down before Him and honoring Him as God and Master, and honoring them for the sake of the common Master, as His closest servants, and rendering unto them relative veneration![^924]

И҆ є҆́же Прр҃ка ва́мъ възста́витъ Гд҃ь Бг҃ъ нашъ ꙗ҆́кѡже менѐ, Мѡѷсе́а гл҃юща разꙋмѣ́ющымъ. Та́же гл҃ющымъ, прїѧ́ти ᲂу҆́бѡ Прр҃ка, не въводѧ́щим же и҆зѡбраже́ньми блг҃ть Прр҃чествꙋ, и҆ всемі́рное сп҃нїе, ꙗ҆́кѡ видѣ́нно бы́сть, ꙗ҆́кѡ съпоживѐ чл҃кѡмъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ стр҃сти и҆ недꙋ́ги и҆сцѣле́нїа лꙋ́чши и҆сцѣлѝ, ꙗ҆́кѡ Распя́тъ бысть, ꙗ҆́кѡ Погребе́нъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ Въскр҃се, ꙗ҆́кѡ всѧ̀ ꙗ҆́же ѡ҆ на́съ пострада́же и҆ сътворѝ. Сїѧ̀ ᲂу҆́бѡ всемї́рнаѧ и҆ сп҃се́ннаѧ дѣла̀ на И҆́кѡнахъ зрѣ́ти непрїе́млющымъ, ни́же чтꙋ́щимъ сїа̀ ни покланя́ющим сѧ: А҆на́ѳема, Три́жды.

items.slavonic_text: Наводѧ́щымъ на неизрече́нное въ пло́ти смотре́нїе Гдⷭа и҆ Бг҃а, и҆ сп҃са на́шегѡ І҆и҃са Хрⷭта́ тщетла́сїѧ нѣ́каѧ. и҆ глаго́лющымъ и҆лѝ мꙋ́дрствꙋющымъ покланя́тися чл҃чтвꙋ Хв҃ꙋ, неприкоснове́ннымъ Бж҃тво́мъ рабо́тнѡ. и҆ рабо́тꙋ присносꙋ́щнꙋю стѧжа́ти, ꙗ҆́кѡже сꙋ́ществе́ннꙋю, и҆ неѿе́млемꙋю: Ана́ѳема, Три́жды.
items.english_text: Unto those who introduce certain vain fancies into the ineffable dispensation in the flesh of our Lord and God and Savior Jesus Christ, and say or hold that the humanity of Christ is worshipped with servile homage by the intangible Godhead, and that it acquired an everlasting servitude as essential and inalienable:[^937]

items.slavonic_text: Глаго́лющымъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ въ вре́мѧ мироспаси́тельныя стра́сти Гдⷭа и҆ Бг҃а, и҆ сп҃са на́шегѡ І҆и҃са Хрⷭта̀ принесе́ннꙋю сп҃се́нїя на́шегѡ ра́ди же́ртвꙋ, чⷭтна́гѡ є҆гѡ̀ Тѣ́ла же и҆ Кро́ви, ꙗ҆́кѡже А҆рхїере́ю по чл҃че́скомꙋ ѡ҆ на́съ оу҆потреблѧ́ющꙋ. Зане́же то́й самъ, и҆ Бг҃ъ, и҆ жре́цъ, и҆ же́ртва, по сла́вному в Бг҃осло́вїи Грїго́рїю, Принесе́ оу҆́бѡ самъ Бг҃ꙋ и҆ Ѻ҆ц҃ꙋ̀. не прїѧ́тъ же ꙗ҆́кѡ Бг҃ъ съ Ѻ҆ц҃е́мъ, са́мъ же Є҆диноро́дный. и҆ Дх҃ъ ст҃ы́й, ꙗ҆́кѡ тѣ́ми ѿчꙋжда́ютъ само́гѡ Бг҃а сло́ва, и҆ є҆диносꙋ́щнагѡ, и҆ є҆диносла́внагѡ, семꙋ̀ оу҆тѣ́шителю Дх҃а, Бголѣ́пнаго є҆диноу҆́тїя же и҆ досто́инства: Ана́ѳема, г҃.
items.english_text: Unto those who do not with all reverence employ the distinction of the mind solely for the showing forth of the difference of the two natures ineffably met together in Christ and united in Him without confusion and without division; but employ that same distinction and say that the assumed nature is other not only in nature but also in dignity, and that it serves God and offers servile worship, and renders diligent honor as a debt, just as the ministering spirits serve and bow down servilely, and who teach that by its proper assumed nature it is High Priest, and not the God-Word inasmuch as He became man, and who through such notions dare apostolically to divide the one Christ our Lord and God:[^938]

provenance.verbatim_source: Unto those who do not with all reverence employ the distinction of the mind solely for the showing forth of the difference of the two natures ineffably met together in Christ and united in Him without confusion and without division; but employ that same distinction and say that the assumed nature is other not only in nature but also in dignity, and that it serves God and offers servile worship, and renders diligent honor as a debt, just as the ministering spirits serve and bow down servilely, and who teach that by its proper assumed nature it is High Priest, and not the God-Word inasmuch as He became man, and who through such notions dare apostolically to divide the one Christ our Lord and God:[^938]

items.slavonic_text: Непрїе́млющымъ на всѧ́къ день приноси́мꙋю Же́ртвꙋ, ѿ прїе́мшыхъ ѿ Хрⷭта̀ Бж҃твенныхъ та́инствъ сщ҃еннодѣ́йствїе, ст҃ѣ́й Трⷪцѣ приноси́тисѧ. ꙗ҆́кѡ противовѣща́телемъ ѿню́дъ сщ҃е́ннымъ и҆ Бж҃твеннымъ Ѻ҆ц҃е́мъ, Васи́лїю же и҆ Златооу҆́стꙋ, и҆́мже
items.english_text: Unto those who say that at the time of the world-saving Passion of our Lord and God and Savior Jesus Christ, the sacrifice of His precious Body and Blood offered for our salvation—as by an High Priest acting according to what is human for our sake, seeing that He is Himself both God, and Priest, and Sacrifice, according to Gregory the renowned in Theology[^939]—was indeed offered by Himself unto God the Father, but was not received as God together with the Father by the Only-begotten Himself and the Holy Spirit, so that thereby they alienate from the God-befitting equal essence and dignity God the Word Himself, and the Comforter Spirit Who is consubstantial and co-glorified with Him:[^940]

provenance.verbatim_source: Unto those who say that at the time of the world-saving Passion of our Lord and God and Savior Jesus Christ, the sacrifice of His precious Body and Blood offered for our salvation—as by an High Priest acting according to what is human for our sake, seeing that He is Himself both God, and Priest, and Sacrifice, according to Gregory the renowned in Theology[^939]—was indeed offered by Himself unto God the Father, but was not received as God together with the Father by the Only-begotten Himself and the Holy Spirit, so that thereby they alienate from the God-befitting equal essence and dignity God the Word Himself, and the Comforter Spirit Who is consubstantial and co-glorified with Him:[^940]

items.english_text: Unto those who do not accept that the Sacrifice offered every day by those who have received from Christ the sacred administration of the Divine Mysteries is offered unto the Holy Trinity, as being utterly in opposition to the sacred and divine Fathers, Basil and Chrysostom, with whom agree also the rest of the God-bearing Fathers in their words and writings:[^941]

provenance.verbatim_source:
Unto those who do not accept that the Sacrifice offered every day by those who have received from Christ the sacred administration of the Divine Mysteries is offered unto the Holy Trinity, as being utterly in opposition to the sacred and divine Fathers, Basil and Chrysostom, with whom...
...agree also the rest of the God-bearing Fathers in their words and writings:[^941]

items.slavonic_text: Слы́шащымъ оу҆́бѡ сп҃са ѡ҆ Сщ҃еннодѣ́йствїи ѿ него̀ пре́данномъ Бж҃твенныхъ та́инствъ, гл҃юща, Сїѐ твори́те въ моѐ воспомина́нїе: Не прїе́млющїи же пра́вѣ воспомина́нїѧ, но дерза́ющїи глаго́лати: ꙗ҆́кѡже ѡ҆бновлѧ́етъ привиди́телнѡ, и҆ ѡ҆́бразнѡ на чⷭтно́мъ Крⷭтѣ̀ ѿ сп҃са на́шегѡ принесе́ннꙋю Же́ртвꙋ, своего́ тѣ́ла же и҆ кро́ви, въ ѡ҆́бщее чл҃чїѧгѡ є҆стества̀, и҆збавле́нїе же и҆ ѡ҆чнще́нїе, на всѧ́къ де́нь приноси́маѧ же́ртва, ѿ Сщ҃еннодѣ́йствоꙋющихъ Бж҃твеннаѧ та́инства. ꙗ҆́кѡже сп҃съ на́шъ, и҆ Влⷣка всѣ́хъ предаде́. и҆ сегѡ́ ра́ди и҆́нꙋ бы́ти сїю̀, ѿ и҆спе́рва сп҃сомъ съверши́вшїѧсѧ въводѧ́щымъ. и҆ къ ѻ҆́ной привиди́телнѡ и҆ ѡ҆́бразнѡ възноси́мꙋю, ꙗ҆́кѡ оу҆́ничижа́ющїи стра́шнагѡ и҆ Бж҃твеннагѡ Сщ҃еннодѣ́йствїа та́инство, и҆́мже бꙋ́дꙋщѧѧ жи́зни ѡ҆брѣ́тенїе прїе́млемъ, и҆ сїѧ Бж҃е́нномꙋ Ѻ҆ц҃ꙋ на́шемꙋ І҆ѡа́ннꙋ Златоꙋ́стомъ ѡ҆бновлѧ́ющꙋ же́ртвы непремѣ́нное, и҆ є҆ди́нꙋ и҆ тꙋ́южде бы́ти гл҃ющꙋ, въ мно́ги Толкованїи рече́нїй вели́кагѡ Па́ѵла: Ана́ѳема, Три́жды.
items.english_text: Unto those who hear indeed the Savior saying concerning the sacred administration of the Divine Mysteries delivered by Him: *Do this in remembrance of Me* (Luke 22:19), but do not accept the remembrance rightly, and dare to say that the sacrifice offered every day by those who minister the Divine Mysteries—as our Savior and Master of all delivered—renews only in appearance and figuratively the Sacrifice of His own Body and Blood offered upon the precious Cross by our Savior for the common redemption and purification of human nature; and who therefore introduce this sacrifice as being another from that which was accomplished from the beginning by the Savior, and referring to that one only in appearance and figuratively, as they that make light of the fearful and divine mystery of the sacred ministration, through which we receive the earnest of the life to come, and this though our divine Father John Chrysostom asserts the unchanging nature of the sacrifice and declares it to be one and the same in many commentaries upon the sayings of the great Paul:[^942]

provenance.verbatim_source: Unto those who hear indeed the Savior saying concerning the sacred administration of the Divine Mysteries delivered by Him: *Do this in remembrance of Me* (Luke 22:19), but do not accept the remembrance rightly, and dare to say that the sacrifice offered every day by those who minister the Divine Mysteries—as our Savior and Master of all delivered—renews only in appearance and figuratively the Sacrifice of His own Body and Blood offered upon the precious Cross by our Savior for the common redemption and purification of human nature; and who therefore introduce this sacrifice as being another from that which was accomplished from the beginning by the Savior, and referring to that one only in appearance and figuratively, as they that make light of the fearful and divine mystery of the sacred ministration, through which we receive the earnest of the life to come, and this though our divine Father John Chrysostom asserts the unchanging nature of the sacrifice and declares it to be one and the same in many commentaries upon the sayings of the great Paul:[^942]

items.slavonic_text: А҆наста́сїю, Кѡнстантоі́нꙋ, и҆ Ники́тѣ, нача́лникомъ въ І҆са́ѵрѣхъ є҆ресе́й, ꙗ҆́кѡ скве́рнымъ, и҆ наста́вникѡмъ поги́бели: Ана́ѳема, г҃.
items.english_text: Unto those who surmise and introduce temporal intervals into the reconciliation of human nature unto the divine and blessed nature of the life-originating and all-spotless Trinity, and who first lay down that we were reconciled unto the only-begotten Word from the very assumption of our nature, and afterwards unto God the Father by the saving Passion of Christ the Savior; and who divide the indivisible, whereas the divine and blessed Father teaches that for the sake of the mystery of the whole dispensation the Only-begotten reconciled us by Himself, and by Himself and in Himself unto God the Father, and consequently in every way unto the all-holy and life-creating Spirit also; as inventors of novel inquiries and alien notions:[^943]

provenance.verbatim_source: Unto those who surmise and introduce temporal intervals into the reconciliation of human nature unto the divine and blessed nature of the life-originating and all-spotless Trinity, and who first lay down that we were reconciled unto the only-begotten Word from the very assumption of our nature, and afterwards unto God the Father by the saving Passion of Christ the Savior; and who divide the indivisible, whereas the divine and blessed Father teaches that for the sake of the mystery of the whole dispensation the Only-begotten reconciled us by Himself, and by Himself and in Himself unto God the Father, and consequently in every way unto the all-holy and life-creating Spirit also; as inventors of novel inquiries and alien notions:[^943]

items.slavonic_text: Па́ѵлꙋ въ Са́ѵла ѡ҆брати́вшомꙋсѧ, и҆ Ѳео́дѡрꙋ нарица́емомꙋ Га́стꙋ, и҆ Стефа́нꙋ Моли́тꙋ. еще же и҆ Ѳео́дѡрꙋ Крїѳі́нꙋ. и҆ Лалꙋ́дїю Левꙋ̀, и҆ к ни́мъ, а҆́ще кто рече́ннымъ подо́бенъ ѕлоче́стїемъ, в ко́емъ либо а҆́ще бы́лъ бы катало́гꙋ, кли́роса, и҆ли досто́инства нѣ́коегѡ, и҆ли начина́нїа, и҆спы́танный, си́мъ всѣ́мъ съпребыва́ющимъ и҆́хъ ѕлоче́стїю: Ана́ѳема, г҃.

items.slavonic_text: Геро́нтїю, въ Сꙋкла́мпѣ оу҆стреми́вшомꙋсѧ, к Крї́тѣ же ꙗ҆́дъ, ненави́стныа своеѧ̀ є҆́реси и҆з̾лїѧвшомꙋ, и҆ ѡ҆каꙗ́ннымъ себѐ прозва́вшомꙋ, ѡ҆ и҆звраще́нїи, оу҆́бы, сп҃се́ннагѡ смотре́нїа Хв҃а, въ превра́тныхъ є҆гѡ̀ оу҆че́нїи, и҆ списа́нїи, и҆ съпрѣ́ѧющимъ є҆мꙋ̀: Ана́ѳема, Три́жды.

items.slavonic_text: Бл҃готѣствова́ти оу҆́бѡ ѡ҆бѣщава́ющымсѧ, злочести́ваѧ же оу҆че́нїѧ є҆́ллинскаѧ, Правосла́вной и҆ собо́рной Це́ркви, ѡ҆ дꙋша́хъ чл҃чкихъ, и҆ нб҃сѝ, и҆ землѝ, и҆ и҆ны́хъ творе́нїихъ безсра́мнѡ, и҆лѝ па́че злочести́вѡ въводѧ́щымъ: Ана́ѳема, Три́жды.

items.slavonic_text: Ве́щество безна́чалное, и҆ І҆де́и и҆ли събезна́чалное съдѣ́телю всѣ́хъ и҆ Бг҃ꙋ оу҆ча́щымъ. и҆ ꙗ҆́кѡ нб҃о и҆ землѧ̀, и҆ про́чаѧ ѡ҆стзда́нїя, присносꙋ́щнаже сꙋ́ть и҆ безна́чална, и҆ пребыва́ютъ непремѣ́нна. И҆ противозаконополага́ютъ ре́кшомꙋ, Нб҃о и҆ земля̀ пре́йдꙋтъ, словеса́ же моѧ̀ не пре́йдꙋтъ. И҆ ѡ҆ землѣ̀ тщетла́вꙋющимъ, и҆ Бж҃твеннꙋю кля́твꙋ на своя̀ главы́ ведꙋ́щим: Ана́ѳема, Три́жды.

items.slavonic_text: Глаго́лющымъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ Є҆́ллинстїи мꙋ́дрецѐ, и҆ пе́рвїи ѿ е҆ресенача́лникѡвъ, ѿ ст҃ы́хъ Седми вселе́нскихъ Собо́рѡвъ, и҆ ѿ всѣ́хъ въ Правосла́вїи проѕїѧ́вшѝ Ѻ҆ц҃ъ, Ана́ѳемѣ положе́нїи, ꙗ҆́кѡ чꙋжи́и Собо́рныя Це́ркве, ра́ди скве́рнагѡ и҆ нечисто́тнагѡ въ словесе́ их преꙋмноже́нїа, лꙋ́чшїи сꙋ́тъ помно́гꙋ, и҆ здѐ, и҆ в бꙋ́дꙋщом сꙋ́дищи: и҆ бл҃гочти́вы оу҆́бѡ и҆ Правосла́вныхъ мꙋже́и, и҆на́кѡ же по стра́сти члове́ческой, и҆ли неразꙋмѣ́нїю прегрѣши́вши: Ана́ѳема, г҃.
items.english_text: Unto those who prefer the vain so-called wisdom of the profane philosophers, and follow their teachers, and accept the transmigration of human souls, or that like unto irrational animals they perish and are reduced unto nothing, and who on this account reject the resurrection, the judgment, and the final retribution of life:[^951]

items.english_text: Unto those who say that the Greek sages and the foremost of the heresiarchs—who were placed under anathema by the holy Seven Ecumenical Councils and by all the Fathers who shone forth in Orthodoxy as alien unto the Catholic Church because of the filth and impurity of their verbiage—are far better, both here and at the future judgment, than pious and Orthodox men who have sinned in some other way through human passion or ignorance:[^953]

items.slavonic_text: Вѣ́рою чи́стою, и҆ про́стою, и҆ цѣлодꙋ́шнымъ срⷣцемъ, сп҃са на́шегѡ и҆ Бг҃а, и҆ Прⷭтыѧ є҆гѡ̀ ро́ждшїѧ Влⷣчца нашеѧ Бц҃а, и҆ про́чихъ ст҃ы́хъ преди́внаѧ чꙋдеса̀, непрїе́млющымъ. но покꙋша́ющымсѧ показа́нми и҆ словесы̀ премꙋ́дростными, ꙗ҆́кѡ немо́щна ѡ҆брѣщѝ, и҆ли по мнѣ́нїи и҆́мъ протолковати, и҆ по своему̀ оу҆мꙋ̀ соста́влити: Ана́ѳема, Є҆ди́нощи.
items.english_text: Unto those who do not accept with a pure and simple faith and with a whole-hearted spirit the marvelous miracles of our Savior and God, and of our Lady the Theotokos who bore Him, and of the rest of the saints; but attempt by sophistical proofs and words to show them impossible, or interpret them according to their own opinion, and configure them according to their own mind:[^954]

provenance.verbatim_source: Unto those who do not accept with a pure and simple faith and with a whole-hearted spirit the marvelous miracles of our Savior and God, and of our Lady the Theotokos who bore Him, and of the rest of the saints; but attempt by sophistical proofs and words to show them impossible, or interpret them according to their own opinion, and configure them according to their own mind:[^954]

items.slavonic_text: Съ и҆ны́ми ба́снеными зда́нїи, ѡ҆ себѐ самѣ́хъ, и҆ на на́съ зда́нїе прездава́ющымъ, и҆ Платони́ческїя Ѻ҆́бразы сꙋ́ществъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ и҆́стинныя прїе́млющымъ. и҆ ꙗ҆́кѡ пакивѣ́щное вещество̀ ѿ ѻ҆́бразѡвъ сꙋ́ществъ и҆з̾ѡбража́етсѧ, глаго́лющымъ, и҆ проѧвле́ннѡ ѿмѣта́ющимъ самовла́стное Содѣ́телѧ, ѿ несꙋ́щагѡ въ бытїе́ приведшагѡ всѧ̀. и҆ ꙗ҆́кѡ Тво́рца всѣ́мъ Нача́ло и҆ Коне́цъ поло́жшаго, вла́стельски и҆ Влⷣчески: Ана́ѳема, Є҆дино́щи.
items.english_text: Unto those who pursue Greek learning, and do not study therein for education only, but follow their vain opinions and believe them as true, and so cleave unto them as having certainty, so as to lead others unto them, sometimes secretly and sometimes openly, and to teach them without hesitation:[^955]

provenance.verbatim_source: Unto those who pursue Greek learning, and do not study therein for education only, but follow their vain opinions and believe them as true, and so cleave unto them as having certainty, so as to lead others unto them, sometimes secretly and sometimes openly, and to teach them without hesitation:[^955]

items.slavonic_text: Прїе́млющымъ и҆ подаю́щымъ тще́тныя и҆ є҆́ллинскїѧ глаго́лы. ꙗ҆́кѡ пребытїе́ є҆́сть дꙋша́мъ, и҆ не ѡ҆ несꙋ́щаго всѧ бы́ша и҆ приведо́шася. ꙗ҆́кѡ коне́цъ є҆́сть мꙋ́цѣ, и҆ли оу҆строе́нїе па́ки зда́нїа и҆ чл҃чкихъ веще́й. и҆ таковы́ми словесы̀ Црⷭтво нб҃ное разрꙋше́нно вся́кѡ, и҆ преходѧ́щее въводѧтъ, є҆го́же вѣ́чнымъ и҆ непостижи́мым самъ Хрⷭто́съ и҆ Бг҃ъ нашъ, навꙋчѝ, и҆ предадѐ. и҆ всѣ́мъ Ве́тхимъ и҆ Но́вымъ писа́нїемъ мы прїѧ́хомъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ и҆ мꙋ́ка безконе́чна є҆́сть, и҆ црⷭтво присносꙋ́щное. Си́цевыми же словесы̀, себе́ же погꙋблѧ́ющимъ, и҆ и҆ны́мъ вѣ́чнаго ѡ҆сꙋжде́нїя вино́внымъ бы́вшимъ: Ана́ѳема, Три́жды.
items.english_text: Unto those who together with other mythical inventions remodel creation of themselves and over us, and accept Platonic Forms of essences as true, and say that material substance is formed from the forms of essences, and openly reject the sovereign will of the Fashioner Who brought all things from non-existence into being, and Who as Creator sovereignly and Masterfully appointed the beginning and end for all:[^956]

provenance.verbatim_source: Unto those who together with other mythical inventions remodel creation of themselves and over us, and accept Platonic Forms of essences as true, and say that material substance is formed from the forms of essences, and openly reject the sovereign will of the Fashioner Who brought all things from non-existence into being, and Who as Creator sovereignly and Masterfully appointed the beginning and end for all:[^956]

items.english_text: Unto those who say that in the final and general resurrection men will rise and be judged with other bodies, and not with those in which they ended the present life, as though these had rotted and perished; and who utter vain and empty babblings against Christ our God Himself, and His Disciples, and our Teachers who have thus taught, that with the same bodies wherein men lived, with them also shall they receive retribution; and moreover when the great Apostle Paul in his discourse on the resurrection showed forth the truth extensively by proofs (1 Cor. 15), and exposed those that thought otherwise as foolish; unto those therefore who enact laws contrary to his commands and teachings:[^957]

items.english_text: Unto those who accept and spread the vain and Greek words that there is a pre-existence of souls, and that not all things were made and brought out of non-existence; that there is an end unto torment, or a restitution of creation and of human affairs; and by such words introduce that the Kingdom of Heaven is altogether dissoluble and transitory, which Christ our God Himself taught and delivered to be eternal and unsearchable, and as we have received through all the Old and New Scripture that both torment is unending and the Kingdom everlasting; and who by such words destroy themselves and become the cause of eternal condemnation unto others:[^958]

items.slavonic_text: Наꙋчи́вшимсѧ злочести́вѡ ѿ Немона́ха Ни́ла, и҆ всѣ́мъ ѡ҆бща́ющымсѧ и҆̀мъ: Ана́ѳема, Три́жды.
items.english_text: Unto those who have learned impiously from the false-monk Nilus, and unto all that have communion with them:[^959]

items.slavonic_text: Прїе́млющимъ и҆́стиннагѡ Бг҃а Гдⷭа и҆ сп҃са на́шегѡ І҆и҃са Хрⷭта́, гла́съ: Ѻ҆ц҃ъ мо́й бо́лїй менѐ є҆́сть: Гла́тнеже, съ про́чїими Толкова́нїи ст҃ы́хъ Ѻ҆те́цъ, и҆ по чл҃чтвꙋ въ не́мъ поє́мꙋже и҆ пострада̀. ꙗ҆́кѡже ꙗ҆́вѣ въ мно́гихъ ѿ Бг҃одꙋхнове́нных слове́съ и҆́хъ, ст҃іи Ѻ҆ц҃ѝ проповѣ́дꙋютъ. Еще же и҆ гл҃ющимъ само́мꙋ Хрⷭтꙋ̀ пло́тїю свое́ю стра́сти: Вѣ́чная па́мѧть, Три́жды.
items.english_text: Unto those who wrongly receive the divine voices of the holy Teachers of God's Church, and attempt otherwise to interpret and pervert that which was spoken clearly and distinctly in them by the grace of the Holy Spirit:[^960]

provenance.verbatim_source: Unto those who wrongly receive the divine voices of the holy Teachers of God's Church, and attempt otherwise to interpret and pervert that which was spoken clearly and distinctly in them by the grace of the Holy Spirit:[^960]

items.slavonic_text: Гл҃ющымъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ пло́ть Гнⷭѧ ѿ того́же соедине́нїя възнесе́ная сѧ. и҆ превы́шше всѧ́кїѧ чтѝ преложе́нная, ꙗ҆́кѡ ѿ кра́йнѧгѡ соедине́нїѧ є҆динобж҃на бы́вши, неѡтмѣ́тнѡ, непремѣ́ннѡ, несли́тнѡ, непрело́жнѡ, ра́ди ѵ҆поста́снагѡ соедине́нїя, и҆ неѡдѣ́лнѡ, и҆ нераздѣ́лнѡ пребыва́ющая, прїе́мшомꙋ ю Бг҃ꙋ сло́вꙋ, равносла́внѡ є҆мꙋ̀ почита́етсѧ, и҆ покланя́етсѧ є҆ди́нѣмъ поклане́нїемъ, и҆ на Црⷭкихъ и҆ Бж҃кїихъ посажда́етъ сѧ мѣ́стѣхъ ѡ҆деснꙋ́ю Бг҃а Ѻ҆ц҃а̀, ꙗ҆́кѡ Бж҃тва̀ възвышенїѧ ѡ҆богаща́ющаѧся, сохранѧ́емымъ сво́йствомъ є҆сте́ствъ: Вѣ́чная па́мять, г҃.
items.english_text: Unto those who accept the voice of the true God, our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ: *My Father is greater than I* (John 14:28), and interpret it, together with the other expositions of the holy Fathers, as spoken according to His humanity in which He suffered, as the holy Fathers clearly proclaim in many of their God-inspired sayings; and furthermore unto those who say that Christ suffered in His own flesh:[^961]

items.slavonic_text: Непрїе́млющымъ гла́са, и҆́стиннагѡ Бг҃а и҆ сп҃са на́шегѡ І҆и҃са Хрⷭта́:
items.english_text: Unto those who understand and proclaim the deification of the assumed nature to be a transformation of human nature into Godhead; and who do not understand that from that same union the Body of the Lord indeed partook of divine dignity and majesty, and is worshipped with one adoration together with God the Word Who assumed it, and is of one honor, of one glory, life-creating, of equal glory with God the Father and the all-holy Spirit, and sharing the same throne, yet that this Body is not consubstantial with God, seeing it remains distinct in the natural properties of the Creator, being circumscribed and possessing the other properties visible in the human nature of Christ; but blend it into the essence of the Godhead, so as to be exalted out of this, or say that the Incarnation of the Lord and His Passions were an appearance and not truth, or that the Only-begotten suffered in His Godhead:[^962]

provenance.verbatim_source: Unto those who understand and proclaim the deification of the assumed nature to be a transformation of human nature into Godhead; and who do not understand that from that same union the Body of the Lord indeed partook of divine dignity and majesty, and is worshipped with one adoration together with God the Word Who assumed it, and is of one honor, of one glory, life-creating, of equal glory with God the Father and the all-holy Spirit, and sharing the same throne, yet that this Body is not consubstantial with God, seeing it remains distinct in the natural properties of the Creator, being circumscribed and possessing the other properties visible in the human nature of Christ; but blend it into the essence of the Godhead, so as to be exalted out of this, or say that the Incarnation of the Lord and His Passions were an appearance and not truth, or that the Only-begotten suffered in His Godhead:[^962]

items.slavonic_text: Непрїе́млющымъ гла́са, и҆́стиннагѡ Бг҃а и҆ сп҃са на́шегѡ І҆и҃са Хрⷭта́:
items.english_text: Unto those who say that the flesh of the Lord, exalted by that same union and set above every honor, as having become deified by the supreme union, unalterably, unchangeably, without confusion, without transmutation, on account of the hypostatic union, and abiding undivided and inseparable from God the Word Who assumed it, is honored with equal glory with Him, and is worshipped with one adoration, and is seated in imperial and divine places at the right hand of God the Father, as being enriched with the exaltations of the Godhead, while the proper characteristics of the natures are preserved:[^963]

provenance.verbatim_source: Unto those who say that the flesh of the Lord, exalted by that same union and set above every honor, as having become deified by the supreme union, unalterably, unchangeably, without confusion, without transmutation, on account of the hypostatic union, and abiding undivided and inseparable from God the Word Who assumed it, is honored with equal glory with Him, and is worshipped with one adoration, and is seated in imperial and divine places at the right hand of God the Father, as being enriched with the exaltations of the Godhead, while the proper characteristics of the natures are preserved:[^963]

items.english_text: Unto those who reject the voices of the holy Fathers that were in harmony concerning the establishment of the right dogmas of God's Church—of Athanasius, Cyril, Ambrose, Amphilochius the God-befitting, of Leo the most holy Archbishop of Old Rome, and the rest; and moreover unto those who do not kiss the acts of the Ecumenical Councils, I say the Fourth and the Sixth:[^964]

items.slavonic_text: Непрїе́млющымъ гла́са, и҆́стиннагѡ Бг҃а и҆ сп҃са на́шегѡ І҆и҃са Хрⷭта́:
items.english_text: Unto those who do not accept the voice of the true God and our Savior Jesus Christ: *My Father is greater than I* (John 14:28), as the saints interpreted this in diverse ways: some indeed saying that it was spoken according to His Godhead, by reason of His caused generation from the Father; while others saying it was according to the natural properties of the flesh assumed by Him and hypostatically united to His Godhead, that is: being created, circumscribed, mortal, and the rest of the natural and blameless passions, on account of which the Lord said that He was less than the Father; but who say that such a voice is to be understood only when in subtle consideration the flesh is understood as separated from the Godhead, as though it were not even united; and unto those who do not accept such a saying according to subtle consideration of division—as was spoken by the holy Fathers at that time when servitude and ignorance are mentioned, as not enduring that the deified and equal flesh of Christ should be insulted by such words; but who say that according to subtle consideration of the assumption the natural properties are not truly existing in the Lord's flesh in the hypostasis of His Godhead and abiding inseparable; and who teach these things concerning non-hypostatic and false things, which apply to hypostatic and true things:[^965]

items.slavonic_text: Сꙋ́щомꙋ Митрополи́тꙋ Ке́ркѵрскомꙋ Кѡнстанти́нꙋ Бꙋлга́рскомꙋ, ѕлѣ̀ и҆ нечести́вѣ оу҆ча́щомꙋ ѡ҆ и҆́стинномъ Бг҃ѣ и҆ сп҃са на́шегѡ І҆и҃с Хрⷭта́ гла́сѣ: Ѻ҆ц҃ъ мо́й бо́лїй менѐ є҆́сть: И҆ немꙋ́дрствꙋющꙋ и҆ глаго́лющꙋ, ꙗ҆́кѡ и҆ по и҆но́мꙋ оу҆́бѡ бл҃гочести́выи разꙋмѣ́нїе прїе́млетсѧ сїѝ ѿ ст҃ы́хъ Бг҃оно́сныхъ Ѻ҆те́цъ, но и҆ по само́й ѿ Є҆диноро́днагѡ Сн҃а Бж҃їѧ прїе́мшейся пло́ти, ѿ ст҃ы́ѧ Дв҃цы и҆ Бц҃ы, и҆ Бж҃тво́мъ є҆гѡ̀ съста́вшейсѧ. несли́тнѡ, съ нераздѣ́лныи соединенїемъ та́ѧжде сво́йства и҆мꙋщой. по ни́хже Ѻ҆ц҃а̀ Гдⷭь бо́льша себѐ и҆менова̀. въ є҆ди́номъ поклане́нїи, съ свои́мъ прїѧ́тїемъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ є҆динобж҃нымъ, и҆ равносла́вным, само́мꙋже Ѻ҆ц҃ꙋ̀, и҆ Всест҃мꙋ́ Дх҃ꙋ, съпокланя́емъ, и҆ съсла́вимъ. Противѧ́щомꙋ же сѧ не подоба́ти разꙋмѣ́тися си́цевомꙋ гла́сꙋ, внегда̀ разꙋмѣва́ется Гдⷭь є҆ди́на ѵ҆поста́сь, соединенныя двѣ̀ є҆стества̀ и҆мѣ́ющи, но внегда̀ по то́нкомꙋ мнѣ́нїи пло́ть прїемлется, раздѣли́шася Бж҃тва̀, и҆ такова́же коего́ждѡ ѿ чл҃вкъ бы́ти разꙋмѣ́ется: И҆ сїа̀ Бг҃осло́внѣйшомꙋ Дамаски́нꙋ, тогда̀ по то́нкомꙋ мнѣ́нїю раздѣле́нїе оу҆ча́щꙋ, внегда̀ гле́тсѧ что ѡ҆ пло́ти Хв҃ой, непреста́телственное, є҆сте́ственнагѡ нѣ́коегѡ сво́йства, но та́блѧтельное рабо́ты и҆ли невѣ́дѣнїя. И҆ нехотя́щомꙋ послѣ́довати сты́мъ Вселе́нскимъ Собо́рѡмъ, Че́твертомꙋ же и҆ Ше́стомꙋ, и҆́же ѡ҆ дво́хъ съединенныи не сли́тнѡ в Хрⷭтѣ̀ є҆сте́ствѣхъ
items.english_text: Unto Constantine the Bulgarian, who was Metropolitan of Corfu, who wickedly and impiously taught concerning the voice of the true God and our Savior Jesus Christ: *My Father is greater than I* (John 14:28); and who did not believe and say that although indeed according to another pious understanding this is received from the holy God-bearing Fathers, yet also according to the very flesh assumed from the holy Virgin and Theotokos by the Only-begotten Son of God and made subsistent in His Godhead, without confusion, having with inseparable union those same properties according to which the Lord called the Father greater than Himself, in one adoration with His assumed nature, as deified and of equal glory, He is worshipped together and glorified together with the Father Himself and the All-Holy Spirit; but who objected that it was not fitting that such a voice should be understood when the Lord is understood as one hypostasis having two united natures, but only when in subtle consideration the flesh is taken as separated from the Godhead and such as to be of any man whatsoever; and this though the most theological Damascene teaches the division in subtle consideration then, when anything is spoken of Christ's flesh that is not abiding, of some natural property, but showing servitude or ignorance; and unto him that would not follow the holy Ecumenical Councils, both the Fourth and the Sixth, which rightly and piously commanded concerning the two natures united without confusion in Christ, and taught the Church of Christ to confess the Orthodox faith; and who thus fell into diverse heresies:[^966]

items.english_text: Unto the most unlearned and false-monk John Eirenikos, and unto the impious writings composed by him, and unto those who kiss these writings, as glorifying and saying that not by reason of the hypostatic and united humanity in our Lord Jesus Christ Himself, the Savior and God, by His Godhead, undivided and inseparable, and without confusion, is His voice in His holy Gospels: *My Father is greater than I* (John 14:28) spoken by Him as perfect Man; but who say that this was spoken by Him according to His humanity only in such wise as when this humanity, stripped bare and in subtle consideration divided in every way from His Godhead, as though it were not united unto Him, is taken as common and ours:[^968]

items.english_text: Unto those who think with them, and say that the Light that shone forth from the Lord at His divine Transfiguration was at one time a phantom and a creature and an apparition that appeared for a little while and was quickly dissolved, and at another time the very essence of God, as into the very most contrary absurdities, and utterly cast themselves down into impossibilities; and on the one hand, raving with the madness of Arius, cut the one Godhead and one God into created and uncreated; and on the other hand, agreeing with the Messalian impiety, say that the divine essence is visible; and do not confess, according to the holy God-inspired theologies of the saints and the pious churchly understanding, that that most divine Light is neither a creature nor the essence of God, but uncreated and natural grace, illumination, and energy, inseparably and ever-existing from that same divine essence:[^979]

items.slavonic_text: Є҆щѐ, си́нми мꙋ́дрствꙋющимъ и҆ глаго́лющымъ, и҆ не є҆ди́ноже дѣ́йство є҆сте́ственное и҆мѣ́ти Бг҃ꙋ, но само́мꙋ сꙋ́ществꙋ бы́ти. сїе́ же и҆ не ра́зное всѧ́кѡ мнѧ́щым же сꙋ́щество Бж҃твенное, и҆ Бж҃твенное дѣ́йство, и҆ ни є҆ди́но разꙋмѣ́тисѧ ѿ ни́хъ по ничесо́мꙋ разли́чїе, но та́жде, ѻ҆́вогда оу҆́бѡ сꙋ́ществꙋ, ѻ҆́вогда же дѣ́йствꙋ глагола́тися. ꙗ҆́кѡ и҆ то́жде безꙋ́мнѣ Бж҃твенное сꙋ́щество вся́чески ѿе́млющим, и҆ в небытїѐ ведꙋ́щымъ. Дѣ́йства бо то́кмѡ небы́тное лиша́тися гли́тъ ѡ҆ рече́нїи Оу҆чт҃лїе Цр҃ко́внїи. Ꙋ҆́же и҆ Саве́лїева болѣ́знꙋющимъ, и҆ дре́внее ѻ҆́ного раздѣле́нїе, и҆ сли́тїе, и҆ слꙋче́нїе въ трїе́хъ ѵ҆поста́сехъ Бж҃тва̀, нн҃ѣ в Бж҃твенномъ сꙋ́ществѣ, и҆ дѣ́йствѣ ѡ҆новля́ти дерза́ющимъ, и҆ подо́бнѡ злоче́стнѡ сїѧ слꙋча́ющимъ. Неисповѣ́дꙋющим же по сты́хъ Бг҃одꙋкнове́ннымъ Бг҃осло́вїамъ, и҆ Цр҃ко́вномъ бл҃гꙋти́вомъ мꙋдрова́нїи, сꙋ́щество же в Бг҃ѣ, и҆ сꙋ́щественное сегѡ̀ дѣ́йство. ꙗ҆́коже и҆ны́и множа́йшыи ѿ сты и҆ па́че и҆же ст҃гѡ и҆ Вселе́нскагѡ Ше́стогѡ Собо́ра ꙗ҆́снѡ ꙗ҆ви́ша, ѡ҆ двои́хъ дѣ́йствахъ Хвы́хъ, Бж҃комъ же и҆ Чл҃чкомъ, и҆ двои́хъ во́лѧхъ, сїе все съчини́вше. Ни́же разꙋмѣ́ти хотя́щымъ, ꙗ҆́коже соединенїе Бж҃твеннагѡ сꙋ́щества и҆ дѣ́йства несли́тное, та́кѡ бы́ти и҆ ра́зньство неѿстꙋ́пное, по и҆но́мꙋ же, и҆ па́че винѣ̀ и҆ виновно́мꙋ, и҆ неприча́стное, и҆ прича́стное, ѻ҆́во оу҆́бѡ сꙋ́щества, ѻ҆́во же дѣ́йства, си́мъ оу҆́бѡ такова́я злоче́ствꙋющимъ: Ана́ѳема, Три́жды.
items.english_text: Furthermore, unto those who think with them and say that God has no natural energy, but is essence alone; and who consider the divine essence and the divine energy to be in no way different, and that there is understood between them no distinction whatever, but that the same is called at one time essence and at another time energy; so that they foolishly take away the divine essence itself in every way, and reduce it unto non-existence; for the Teachers of the Church say that only non-existence is deprived of energy; and who are sick with the disease of Sabellius, and dare now to renew in the divine essence and energy his ancient division, confusion, and blending in the three hypostases of the Godhead, and similarly and impiously blend these together; and do not confess, according to the God-inspired theologies of the saints and the pious understanding of the Church, both essence in God and the essential energy thereof, as many others of the saints and especially those of the holy and Ecumenical Sixth Council clearly showed forth concerning the two energies of Christ, divine and human, and the two wills, having composed all this; and who are not willing to understand that as the union of the divine essence and energy is unconfused, so also their distinction is inseparable, in another manner, and especially as cause and caused, and incommunicable and communicable—the one indeed of essence, and the other of energy; unto those therefore who think such impious things:[^980]

items.slavonic_text: Є҆щѐ, съгласꙋ́ющимъ и҆́мъ и҆ глаго́лющымъ, създа́ннꙋю бы́ти всѧ́кꙋю є҆сте́ственнꙋю си́лꙋ и҆ дѣ́йство, Трїѵпоста́сногѡ Бж҃тва̀, ꙗ҆́кѡ създа́ннꙋ ѿ сегѡ̀ всѧ́кѡ, и҆ са́мое Бж҃твенное, сꙋ́щество понꙋжда́ющимъ сла́вити. зда́нное бо по сты́мъ дѣ́йство, зда́нное ꙗ҆ви́тъ є҆́ство. нес҃зда́нное же нес҃зда́нное начертава́ет сꙋ́щество. И҆ ѿсю́дꙋже оу҆жѐ сꙋди́телнымъ въ безбо́жїе всѧ́кѡ
items.english_text: Furthermore, unto those who agree with them and say that every natural power and energy of the Tri-hypostatic Godhead is created, so that from this they are compelled in every way to proclaim the very divine essence also to be created; for according to the saints a created energy manifests a created nature, but an uncreated energy outlines an uncreated essence; and who from this are already judged in every way to fall into godlessness and to append Greek fable-telling and the worship of creatures unto the holy and spotless Christian Faith; and who do not confess, according to the holy God-inspired theologies of the saints and the pious churchly understanding, that every natural power and energy of the Tri-hypostatic Godhead is uncreated:[^981]

items.slavonic_text: Є҆щѐ съгласꙋ́ющимъ и҆̀мъ и҆ глаго́лющимъ, сложе́нїе нѣ́кое всѧ́кѡ ра́ди си́хъ бы́ти в Бг҃ѣ. невѣ́рꙋющимъ же оу҆чн҃їю сты́хъ и҆ не є҆ди́ноже сложе́нїе ѿ є҆сте́ственныхъ в є҆сте́ствѣ бы́ти оу҆ча́щимъ, и҆ ѿсю́дꙋ, не то́кмѡ на на́съ, но и҆ на сты́хъ всѣ́хъ клевещꙋ́тъ, ꙗ҆́вѣ въ мно́гихъ мно́гажды оу҆ча́щимъ, тогда̀ про́стое в Бг҃ѣ и҆ не сло́жное. и҆ Бж҃твеннагѡ сꙋ́щества и҆ дѣ́йства разли́чїе, ꙗ҆́кѡ по ничесо́мꙋ вся́кѡ разли́чїе сїѐ вредѧ́щее Бж҃твенной простотѣ̀. не бо оу҆́бѡ та́кѡ ꙗ҆́вѣ себѣ̀ проти́внаѧ Богосло́вити начина́хꙋ. такова́ѧ оу҆́бѡ тщеслове́ствꙋющимъ. Не и҆сповѣ́дꙋющимъ же, по Бг҃одꙋкнове́ннымъ ст҃ы́мъ Бг҃осло́вїемъ, и҆ бл҃гтїи́вое мꙋдрова́нїе Цр҃ко́вное съ Бг҃оподо́бнымъ си́мъ разли́чїемъ, Бж҃твеннꙋю простотꙋ̀ вельмѝ до́брѣ съхранѧ́ти: Ана́ѳема, Три́жды.
items.english_text: Furthermore, unto those who agree with them and say that by reason of these things there is in every way a certain composition in God; and who do not believe the teaching of the saints who teach that no composition whatsoever from what is natural exists in the divine nature, and who from this sally forth to slander not only us, but also all the saints who clearly teach in many places and many times that God is simple and uncompounded, and that the distinction between the divine essence and energy in no way whatever harms the divine simplicity; for they would not have begun so clearly to theologize things contrary to themselves; unto those therefore who speak such vain words, and do not confess, according to the God-inspired theologies of the saints and the pious churchly understanding, that with this God-befitting distinction divine simplicity is right well preserved:[^982]

items.slavonic_text: Є҆щѐ, си́нми мꙋ́дрствꙋющим, и҆ глаго́лющимъ, причаща́телномꙋ Бж҃твенномꙋ сꙋ́ществꙋ бы́ти, ꙗ҆́кѡ Массалїа́нское злоче́стїе въ Цр҃квъ нашꙋ оу҆жѐ въводи́ти не несрамля́ющїи сѧ, дре́вле тако́вое мнѣ́нїе болѣ́зновавшихъ. Неисповѣ́дꙋющимъ же по Бг҃одꙋхнове́ннымъ бг҃осло́вїем ст҃ыхъ, и҆ бл҃гтїи́вомꙋ Цр҃ко́вномꙋ мꙋдрова́нїю, неѡб̾е́млемꙋ оу҆́бѡ сїю бы́ти, всѧ́кѡ и҆ неприча́стнꙋ, прича́стнꙋ же Бж҃їю бл҃гть же, и҆ дѣ́йство: Ана́ѳема, Три́жды.
items.english_text: Furthermore, unto those who think with them and say that the name 'Godhead' is applied unto the divine essence alone; and who do not confess, according to the God-inspired theologies of the saints and the pious understanding of the Church, that this name is applied no less unto the divine energy, and so again in all ways honor the one Godhead of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, whether someone calls their essence or their energy 'Godhead,' as the divine mystagogues taught us:[^983]

items.slavonic_text: I҆саа́кꙋ нарица́ющомꙋся, А҆ргѵ́рїю, пре всѐ житїе́ болѣ́зновавшомꙋ болѣ́знїю Варлаа́мовою, и҆ А҆кинді́новою, а҆́ще и҆ на концѝ жи́зни своеѧ́, ꙗ҆́кѡже и҆ пе́рвѣе мно́жицею ѿ Цр҃кве Хв҃ы ѡ҆браще́нїе ѡ҆бѣща́вшомꙋ и҆ покаа́нїе, пребыва́ющомꙋже в злоче́стїи, и҆ ѕлѣ̀ дꙋшꙋ свою̀ въ и҆сповѣ́данїи є҆́реси и҆з̾ве́ргшомꙋ: Ана́ѳема, г҃.
items.english_text: Furthermore, unto those who think with them and say that the divine essence is communicable, who do not blush to introduce into our Church the Messalian impiety of those who anciently were sick with such an opinion; and who do not confess, according to the God-inspired theologies of the saints and the pious churchly understanding, that it is incomprehensible and in every way incommunicable, but that divine grace and energy is communicable:[^984]

items.english_text: Unto Gregory, the most holy Metropolitan of Thessalonica, who synodically in the Great Church destroyed Barlaam and Akindynos, the ringleaders and inventors of new heresies, together with their wicked fellowship—who dared to call the natural and indivisible energy and power of God, and simply all the natural properties of the Holy Trinity together, created things, and the unapproachable Light of the Godhead that shone forth on the Mount from Christ a created Godhead, and who began evilly to introduce again into the Church Platonic forms and Greek fables...[^998] and into the Church of Christ; and who very wisely and manfully championed the common, true, and unerring commands of the Church of Christ concerning the Godhead, both by writings, and words, and discourses; and who proclaimed, according to the Divine Scriptures, not one Godhead only, but one God in three Hypostases, active, willing, all-powerful, uncreated in all respects; and who preached the Theologians and expositors of these things—I mean Athanasius, Basil, Gregory, and John Chrysostom,[^999] and Cyril in addition to them, and Maximus the most wise, and the God-proclaiming [John] of Damascus; and who showed himself both in words and deeds to be not only [a follower] of these, but also of the other Fathers and Teachers of Christ's Church, a companion, fellow-traveler, harmonizer, zealous confessor of all these:

items.slavonic_text: Цр҃кви Хв҃ѣ. ѡ҆́бщїѧ же Хв҃ы Цр҃кви, и҆́стинныи и҆ непогрѣши́телныи ѡ҆ бж҃твѣ̀ веле́нїи, мꙋ́дрѡ и҆ мꙋ́жественнѡ зѣ́лѡ во́инствовавшемꙋ, и҆ списа́нїи, и҆ словесы̀, и҆ бесѣ́дами, не є҆ди́но Бж҃тво̀, и҆ Бг҃а є҆дина́го Трїѵпоста́снагѡ, дѣ́йствителнагѡ, воли́телнагѡ, всеси́лнагѡ, несозда́ннагѡ ра́ди всѣ́хъ по Бж҃твенныхъ Писа́нїихъ. И҆ Бг҃осло́вѡвъ же и҆ сказа́телей си́хъ, проповѣ́давшаго, А҆ѳана́сїа гл҃ю, Васи́лїа, Григѡ́рїа, и҆ І҆ѡа́нна Златогнѣ́вагѡ. Кѵрі́лла же к си̑мъ, и҆ Ма́ѯіма премд҃раго. и҆ и҆́же Дама́ску Бг҃оглаго́ливаго. Не то́кмѡ же, но и҆ про́чихъ Ѻ҆тє́цъ, и҆ Ѹ҆чт҃лей Хв҃ы Цр҃кви, и҆ ѡ҆бщи́телѧ, и҆ спꙋ́тника, и҆ согла́сника, и҆ тща́телна, и҆сповѣ́дника, всѣ́хъ си́хъ ꙗ҆́вльшомꙋсѧ и҆ словесы̀ и҆ ве́щьми: Вѣ́чнаѧ па́мѧть, Трї́жды. Всѣ́мъ, ѡ҆ правосла́вїи сподвиза́ющимсѧ, приснопа́мѧтномꙋ, и҆ блаже́нномꙋ семꙋ̀ Царю̀. и҆ сни́мъ и҆ словесы̀ и҆ бесѣ́дами: списа́нїи же и҆ оу҆че́нїи, и҆ всѧ́кимъ словесе́мъ и҆ ве́щїю, мꙋ́жественнѡ предста́телствꙋющимъ ѡ҆ Хв҃ѣй Цр҃кви. и҆ лꙋка́выѧ же и҆ многови́дныѧ є҆́реси, Варлаа́ма же и҆ А҆кинді́на, и҆ є҆диномꙋ́дрны ѡ҆́нѣмъ ѿ Цр҃кви и҆з̾ѡбличи́вшихъ же, и҆ и҆згна́вшихъ в кꙋ́пѣ. А҆пл҃скїа же и҆ Ѻ҆т҃чїа Бл҃гчтїа веле́нїа ꙗ҆́кѡ проповѣ́давшихъ. И҆ сегѡ̀ ра́ди ѕлѣ̀ слы́шавшихъ ѿ злосла́вныхъ, и҆ ѡ҆клевета́вшихъ, и҆ досажда́ющихъ сщ҃еннымъ Бг҃осло́вѡмъ, и҆ Бг҃оно́снымъ Ѻ҆ц҃емъ на́шимъ и҆ Ѹ҆чт҃лемъ: Вѣ́чнаѧ па́мѧть, Трї́жды. И҆сповѣ́дꙋющимъ є҆дина́го Бг҃а Трїѵпоста́снагѡ, всеси́лнаго, не то́кмѡ несозда́нна по сꙋ́ществꙋ, и҆ ѵ҆поста́сє, но и҆ по дѣ́йствꙋ. И҆ гл҃ющимъ, пребы́ти оу҆́бѡ Бж҃твенное дѣ́йство ѿ Бж҃твеннагѡ сꙋ́щества, пребы́ти же нераздѣ́лнѡ. ра́ди же оу҆́бѡ є҆́же пребы́ти неизрече́нное разсꙋжде́нїе преставлѧ́ющимъ. ра́ди же є҆́же нераздѣ́лнѡ, преесте́ственное показꙋющимъ соединенїе, ꙗ҆́кѡже и҆ ст҃ы́й Вселе́нскїй Ше́стый Собо́ръ ꙗ҆вѝ: Вѣ́чнаѧ па́мѧть, г҃. И҆сповѣ́дꙋющимъ Бг҃а, ꙗ҆́кѡже по сꙋ́ществꙋ несозда́нна и҆ безна́чална, та́кѡже и҆ по дѣ́йствꙋ, безна́чалнагѡ ꙗ҆́вѣ не по вре́меномꙋ прїе́млема, и҆ по Бж҃твенномꙋ оу҆́бѡ сꙋ́ществꙋ, неприча́стнаго и҆ недомы́слителнаго всѧ́кѡ Бг҃а гл҃ющимъ. прича́стна же бы́ти є҆гѡ̀ досто́йнымъ, по Бж҃твенномꙋ и҆ Бг҃отво́рномꙋ дѣ́йствꙋ, ꙗ҆́кѡже Цр҃ко́вныи Бг҃осло́вци гл҃ютъ: Вѣ́чнаѧ па́мѧть, г҃. items.slavonic_text: Цр҃кви Хв҃ѣ. ѡ҆́бщїѧ же Хв҃ы Цр҃кви, и҆́стинныи и҆ непогрѣши́телныи ѡ҆ бж҃твѣ̀ веле́нїи, мꙋ́дрѡ и҆ мꙋ́жественнѡ зѣ́лѡ во́инствовавшемꙋ, и҆ списа́нїи, и҆ словесы̀, и҆ бесѣ́дами, не є҆ди́но Бж҃тво̀, и҆ Бг҃а є҆дина́го Трїѵпоста́снагѡ, дѣ́йствителнагѡ, воли́телнагѡ, всеси́лнагѡ, несозда́ннагѡ ра́ди всѣ́хъ по Бж҃твенныхъ Писа́нїихъ. И҆ Бг҃осло́вѡвъ же и҆ сказа́телей си́хъ, проповѣ́давшаго, А҆ѳана́сїа гл҃ю, Васи́лїа, Григѡ́рїа, и҆ І҆ѡа́нна Златогнѣ́вагѡ. Кѵрі́лла же к си̑мъ, и҆ Ма́ѯіма премд҃раго. и҆ и҆́же Дама́ску Бг҃оглаго́ливаго. Не то́кмѡ же, но и҆ про́чихъ Ѻ҆тє́цъ, и҆ Ѹ҆чт҃лей Хв҃ы Цр҃кви, и҆ ѡ҆бщи́телѧ, и҆ спꙋ́тника, и҆ согла́сника, и҆ тща́телна, и҆сповѣ́дника, всѣ́хъ си́хъ ꙗ҆́вльшомꙋсѧ и҆ словесы̀ и҆ ве́щьми: Вѣ́чнаѧ па́мѧть, Трї́жды. Всѣ́мъ, ѡ҆ правосла́вїи сподвиза́ющимсѧ, приснопа́мѧтномꙋ, и҆ блаже́нномꙋ семꙋ̀ Царю̀. и҆ сни́мъ и҆ словесы̀ и҆ бесѣ́дами: списа́нїи же и҆ оу҆че́нїи, и҆ всѧ́кимъ словесе́мъ и҆ ве́щїю, мꙋ́жественнѡ предста́телствꙋющимъ ѡ҆ Хв҃ѣй Цр҃кви. и҆ лꙋка́выѧ же и҆ многови́дныѧ є҆́реси, Варлаа́ма же и҆ А҆кинді́на, и҆ є҆диномꙋ́дрны ѡ҆́нѣмъ ѿ Цр҃кви и҆з̾ѡбличи́вшихъ же, и҆ и҆згна́вшихъ в кꙋ́пѣ. А҆пл҃скїа же и҆ Ѻ҆т҃чїа Бл҃гчтїа веле́нїа ꙗ҆́кѡ проповѣ́давшихъ. И҆ сегѡ̀ ра́ди ѕлѣ̀ слы́шавшихъ ѿ злосла́вныхъ, и҆ ѡ҆клевета́вшихъ, и҆ досажда́ющихъ сщ҃еннымъ Бг҃осло́вѡмъ, и҆ Бг҃оно́снымъ Ѻ҆ц҃емъ на́шимъ и҆ Ѹ҆чт҃лемъ: Вѣ́чнаѧ па́мѧть, Трї́жды. И҆сповѣ́дꙋющимъ, просїѧ́вшїй неизрече́ннѡ свѣ́тъ на Горѣ̀ Гн҃ѧ Преѡбраже́нїа, свѣ́тъ неприкоснове́нный бы́ти, и҆ свѣ́тъ ве́лїй, и҆ и҆злїѧ́нїе недомы́слителное Бж҃твенныѧ свѣ́тлости, и҆ сла́вꙋ неизрече́ннꙋю, и҆ Бж҃тва сла́вꙋ пресоверше́ннꙋю,
items.english_text: Unto those who confess one God in three Hypostases, all-powerful, not only uncreated according to essence and hypostasis, but also according to energy; and who say that the Divine energy indeed proceeds from the Divine essence, yet proceeds indivisibly; for by proceeding they signify an ineffable distinction, but by indivisibility they demonstrate a supernatural union, even as the holy Sixth Ecumenical Council showed:[^1001]

items.english_text: Unto those who confess that the Light which shone forth ineffably upon the Mount of the Lord's Transfiguration is unapproachable light, and great light, and an incomprehensible outpouring of Divine radiance, and ineffable glory, and the all-perfect glory of the Godhead, and and transcendent, and the timeless glory of the Son, and of the Kingdom of God, and true beauty, and that which is beloved concerning the Divine and blessed nature, and the natural glory of God, and the Godhead of the Father and the Spirit shining forth in the Only-begotten Son, as our Divine and God-bearing Fathers said: Athanasius, and Basil the Great, Gregory the Theologian, and John Chrysostom, and furthermore John of Damascus; and who for these reasons glorify this most divine Light as uncreated:[^1003]
